Caching certificate chains and using a pre-distributed ML-KEM key reduces the handshake to 6.1 kB and 44 ms of device computation.
conclusion: Hybrid P-256+ML-KEM-512 key exchange with a cached device chain fits current message limits and protects session keys against harvest-now-decrypt-later attacks, while full post-quantum migration requires protocol and transport redesign.

title: Spectral Optimization Of Spherical Lattices And Applications To Classical And Quantum Interacting Spin Systems
authors: Jonas V\"oller, Grigorios Makris, Fabian Hassler, Stefan Wessel
abstract: ArXiv:2610.12663v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop an optimization algorithm for spherical lattice discretizations based on the spectrum of the discretized Laplace operator. Starting from refined icosahedral lattices, we minimize the splitting of the [MATH], [MATH], continuum multiplets expected from [MATH] symmetry via gradient descent. This approach simultaneously produces lattices based on triangles with nearly uniform circumradii and perimeters. Although the optimization uses only the free-particle spectrum, we show that the resulting lattices carry over to interacting models. On the optimized lattices, rotational symmetry is restored for the critical Ising and Potts models and primary scaling dimensions are accurately reproduced for the three-dimensional Ising conformal field theory, when appropriate geometry-dependent interaction strengths are used. Higher-angular-momentum descendant states reveal weak residual symmetry breaking beyond the sectors protected by the underlying icosahedral symmetry.
tldr: The paper develops a spectral optimization algorithm for spherical lattice discretizations to restore rotational symmetry and accurately reproduce conformal field theory scaling dimensions in critical Ising and Potts models.
motivation: Spherical lattices derived from icosahedral discretizations suffer from symmetry breaking that limits their use in simulating continuum and conformal field theories.
method: The authors minimize the splitting of continuum SO(3) multiplets of the discretized Laplace operator via gradient descent, producing nearly uniform triangular lattices that are then applied to interacting spin models with geometry-dependent couplings.
result: The optimized lattices restore rotational symmetry for critical Ising and Potts models and reproduce primary scaling dimensions of the 3D Ising CFT, with weak residual symmetry breaking only in higher-angular-momentum descendant states.
conclusion: The optimized spherical lattices provide improved discretizations for studying critical phenomena and conformal field theories in classical and quantum spin systems.

title: All-optical Deconvolution Via Quantum Cross-correlation Spectroscopy With Bright Twin Beams
authors: Yujiro Eto
abstract: ArXiv:2610.13074v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The resolution of spectroscopic measurements is fundamentally limited by the convolution between a system's intrinsic response and the instrument response function, creating an ill-posed inverse problem. While entangled photons can theoretically bypass these limits, low photon flux has hindered their experimental realization. Here, we propose quantum cross-correlation spectroscopy (QCCS), utilizing macroscopic twin beams (signal and idler beams) to physically circumvent this convolution limit in coherent anti-Stokes Raman scattering. Employing the signal beam as a broadband probe, QCCS achieves all-optical deconvolution through a correlation-enhanced sum-frequency generation channel between the convoluted anti-Stokes and idler beams. By subtracting the uncorrelated background using a 500-femtosecond temporal window, we successfully retrieve narrow Raman bands (8 cm^{-1} and 15 cm^{-1}) completely obscured by a 75 cm^{-1} probe bandwidth without numerical deconvolution or prior knowledge. Our results establish macroscopic quantum correlations as a robust resource for high-fidelity spectroscopy, paving the way for ultrashort-pulse-free operando studies under natural, incoherent excitation conditions.
tldr: The paper proposes all-optical quantum cross-correlation spectroscopy using bright twin beams to overcome convolution-limited resolution in coherent anti-Stokes Raman scattering without numerical deconvolution.
motivation: Spectroscopic resolution is fundamentally limited by the convolution of intrinsic and instrument responses, which creates an ill-posed inverse problem; entangled photons can bypass this but typically suffer from low flux.
method: The authors use macroscopic twin beams (signal and idler) with the signal as a broadband probe and exploit correlation-enhanced sum-frequency generation between the convoluted anti-Stokes and idler beams, subtracting uncorrelated background via a 500-fs temporal window.
result: Narrow Raman bands of 8 cm^{-1} and 15 cm^{-1} obscured by a 75 cm^{-1} probe bandwidth are retrieved without numerical deconvolution or prior knowledge.
conclusion: Macroscopic quantum correlations provide a robust resource for high-fidelity spectroscopy, enabling ultrashort-pulse-free operando studies under natural incoherent excitation.

title: Theory Of Disorder-Induced Multimode Coupling In A Fabry-P\'erot Cavity
authors: Hsing-Ta Chen Wei-Kuo Li
abstract: ArXiv:2610.12687v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Strong light--matter interactions have attracted significant interest in physical chemistry due to the potential for modifying molecular processes by hybridizing with cavity photons and forming polaritonic states. However, for a disordered molecular ensemble within an optical cavity capable of supporting multiple photon modes, theoretical understanding of multimode polaritons remains incomplete, particularly regarding whether and how distinct photon modes are mutually coupled through molecules. In this work, we generalize the collective mode expansion formalism to incorporate multiple photonic modes and show that spatial and orientational disorder in the light--matter coupling strength (originating from dipole orientation fluctuations and photonic field inhomogeneity) can mediate cross-mode coupling. This disorder-induced coupling allows for energy transfer to otherwise unexcited photon modes through a mechanism termed disorder-induced multimode activation (DIMA). Using an effective one-dimensional Fabry--P\'erot cavity as a test system, we demonstrate that the cross-mode energy transfer through DIMA can be controlled by changing the molecular layer thickness and the optical properties of the mirrors. Furthermore, we show that DIMA is robust against weak energetic disorder. This mechanistic understanding lays the foundation for a systematic control of multimode photon coupling using disorder-induced effects.
tldr: The paper develops a theory of disorder-induced coupling between multiple photonic modes in a Fabry-Pérot cavity filled with a disordered molecular ensemble, enabling multimode energy transfer.
motivation: Strong light-matter interactions can modify molecular processes via polaritonic states, but the role of multimode coupling in disordered molecular cavities is not well understood.
method: The authors generalize the collective mode expansion formalism to multiple photonic modes and include spatial and orientational disorder in the light-matter coupling, using an effective one-dimensional Fabry-Pérot cavity as a test system.
result: Disorder mediates cross-mode coupling, allowing energy transfer to otherwise unexcited photon modes (disorder-induced multimode activation), which is controllable via molecular layer thickness and mirror optical properties and robust against weak energetic disorder.
conclusion: The mechanistic understanding provides a foundation for controlling multimode photon coupling through disorder-induced effects in molecular polaritonics.

title: An Elementary Approach To The Szeg\H{o} Theorems
authors: Ravisankar Rajagopal Israel Klich
abstract: ArXiv:2610.12724v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The strong Szeg theorem and the Fisher-Hartwig formula describe the asymptotic behavior of determinants obtained by restricting translationally invariant operators to large finite regions. In particular, Szeg's theorem states that, beyond the leading extensive contribution to such a determinant, there is a universal finite correction, [MATH] where [MATH] are the Fourier coefficients of the logarithm of the symbol. Although this formula appears throughout analysis and mathematical physics, the origin of its quadratic form and of the weight [MATH] is often obscured in its standard analytic derivations. We develop an elementary picture in which the strong Szeg term arises from boundary leakage: paths contributing to the matrix exponential leave the finite interval and subsequently return. Counting the shortest such excursions immediately produces the factor [MATH]. We then show that an isolated boundary contributes exactly one half of the strong Szeg correction, while the two boundaries of a long interval decouple. For finite-range matrices this gives a rigorous and intuitive elementary derivation of the asymptotics, with extensions to sufficiently rapidly decaying interactions. A complementary free-fermion argument provides a physical interpretation of the same cancellation mechanism. Numerical examples illustrate the asymtotics in the well controlled regime, the Fisher Hartwig logarithmic correction. The boundary formulation does not itself require translation invariance and therefore suggests natural extensions to disordered systems, higher dimensions, and symbols with internal matrix structure. To illustrate this we numerically go beyond the formal applicability region of the Szeg formula, considering slow decay and disordered cases, and showing in some cases a robustness of the approach even for slowly decaying but disordered potentials.
tldr: The paper gives an elementary, boundary-leakage derivation of the strong Szegő theorem and Fisher-Hartwig formula for Toeplitz determinants.
motivation: Standard analytic derivations of the Szegő correction obscure the origin of its quadratic form and weight, motivating a more intuitive and rigorous combinatorial approach.
method: The authors count shortest excursions of paths that leave and re-enter the finite interval in the matrix exponential, and complement this with a free-fermion argument for the cancellation mechanism.
result: They rigorously derive the asymptotics for finite-range matrices and rapidly decaying interactions, showing a single boundary contributes half the correction and two boundaries decouple; numerics illustrate Fisher-Hartwig logarithmic corrections and robustness for slow decay and disorder.
conclusion: The boundary formulation does not require translation invariance, suggesting natural extensions to disordered systems, higher dimensions, and symbols with internal matrix structure.

title: A Sklar-Type Decomposition For Positive Binary Distributions And A Gibbs Interpretation
authors: Yi-Yu Lin
abstract: ArXiv:2610.12805v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study strictly positive multivariate binary distributions by separating one-body marginals from dependence. Local positive reweighting defines a dependence nucleus, completely characterized by the higher-order Walsh log-linear coefficients [MATH], [MATH]. Any such nucleus and any strictly positive one-body marginals determine a unique joint distribution. In finite-spin Gibbs systems, these coefficients are the many-body interaction couplings.
tldr: The paper develops a Sklar-type decomposition for strictly positive multivariate binary distributions, separating one-body marginals from higher-order dependence via Walsh log-linear coefficients and interpreting them as Gibbs interaction couplings.
motivation: To disentangle marginal effects from dependence in multivariate binary data and connect probabilistic decompositions to Gibbs/Boltzmann descriptions.
method: Uses local positive reweighting to define a dependence nucleus characterized by higher-order Walsh log-linear coefficients, and proves that the nucleus plus one-body marginals uniquely determine the joint distribution.
result: Any strictly positive one-body marginals and any dependence nucleus determine a unique joint distribution; in finite-spin Gibbs systems these coefficients are exactly the many-body interaction couplings.
conclusion: Provides a decomposition with a Gibbs interpretation, linking binary distribution dependence to interaction couplings in statistical mechanics.

title: Quantum-Circuit Residuals For Receptor Functional Potency Prediction: Predictive Gains And Quadratic Structure
authors: Chenyan Jia, Yaping Ma, Yuen Wang, Cong Guo
abstract: ArXiv:2610.13037v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The predictive performance of neural networks for receptor functional potency modeling depends on both molecular representations and prediction-head design. Using GLP-1R cAMP-related pEC50 prediction as the primary task, we jointly train a classical molecular encoder with a linear base head and a shallow quantum-circuit residual head that share the learned molecular representation. We evaluate the models using random and structure-group splits, include tuned Chemprop as a domain reference, and extend the evaluation to ADRB2 and MC4R. Under the GLP-1R structure-group split, the quantum-residual models reduce mean absolute error relative to the corresponding base models from 0.677 to 0.639 with a multilayer perceptron (MLP) encoder and from 0.680 to 0.641 with a graph neural network (GNN) encoder. In structural control experiments, a parameter-count-matched real-orthogonal control achieves similar predictive performance, suggesting that some quantum-residual gains may be associated with structured quadratic feature interactions. By combining receptor functional potency prediction with structural analysis of the quantum residual, this study provides empirical evidence to inform compact residual-head design and highlights the potential of quantum-circuit parameterizations for this task.
tldr: This paper explores quantum-circuit residual heads for receptor functional potency prediction, finding modest predictive gains that are partly attributable to structured quadratic feature interactions rather than uniquely quantum effects.
motivation: The authors aim to improve molecular property prediction for GLP-1R, ADRB2, and MC4R by adding a quantum-circuit residual head to classical molecular encoders, testing whether quantum parameterizations offer benefits for modeling receptor functional potency.
method: They jointly train a classical molecular encoder (MLP or GNN) with a linear base head and a shallow quantum-circuit residual head, evaluate on random and structure-group splits, include Chemprop as a domain reference, and run a parameter-count-matched real-orthogonal control to probe whether gains arise from quadratic feature interactions.
result: Under the GLP-1R structure-group split, quantum-residual models reduce MAE from 0.677 to 0.639 (MLP encoder) and from 0.680 to 0.641 (GNN encoder), but a parameter-matched real-orthogonal control achieves similar performance, suggesting the gains may be largely due to structured quadratic interactions.
conclusion: The study provides empirical evidence for compact residual-head design and highlights potential quantum-circuit parameterizations for receptor potency prediction, while indicating that the observed gains are not uniquely quantum in origin.

title: Block Encoding Of Semiseparable Matrices Via Their Generators
authors: Giacomo Antonioli, Gianna M. Del Corso, Roel van Beeumen
abstract: ArXiv:2610.13228v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present an explicit quantum circuit that constructs a block encoding of a generator-representable semiseparable (one-pair) matrix directly from its two generators. For an [MATH] semiseparable matrix with [MATH], the circuit uses [MATH] ancilla qubits and has [MATH] depth, and it realizes a [MATH]-block encoding, where [MATH] is controlled by the accuracy of the state-preparation routines that load the generators. The building blocks of the circuit are cyclic shifts, swaps, and Hadamard gates, each admitting an efficient implementation through the binary decomposition of the relevant indices.
tldr: The paper presents an explicit quantum circuit that block-encodes a generator-representable semiseparable matrix directly from its two generators.
motivation: Block encoding is a key primitive in quantum algorithms, and constructing it efficiently for structured matrices such as semiseparable matrices can enable faster quantum linear algebra routines.
method: The authors design a quantum circuit using cyclic shifts, swaps, and Hadamard gates for efficient binary index decomposition, achieving an ancilla count and depth that depend on the generator parameters.
result: For an M × N semiseparable matrix with a given rank/block structure, the circuit uses O(log(MN)) ancilla qubits and O(log(MN)) depth, realizing a block encoding with accuracy controlled by state-preparation routines for the generators.
conclusion: The construction provides a direct and efficient block encoding for semiseparable matrices, potentially useful for quantum algorithms that exploit matrix structure.

title: Riemannian Hessian Analysis Of Sobolev Gradient Flows For The Gross--Pitaevskii Ground State Problem
authors: Xiangxiong Zhang Shixin Zheng
abstract: ArXiv:2610.12833v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Sobolev gradient flows for the Gross--Pitaevskii ground state problem are Riemannian gradient descent methods on the sphere under a metric induced by a discrete elliptic operator. We analyze their convergence through the condition number of the Riemannian Hessian at the ground state. Bounds of the Rayleigh quotient of the Riemannian Hessian give a uniform analysis of these methods for different metrics. The uniform analysis applies to the classical metrics, such as the shifted Laplacian and the energy-adaptive metrics. Inspired by this analysis, we also consider three new metrics. One of them is a Thomas--Fermi metric, whose condition number is bounded uniformly in the interaction strength for the one-dimensional harmonic trap and whose iteration count does not grow in the Thomas--Fermi regime in the numerical tests. The performance suggested by our analysis is consistent with three-dimensional numerical tests with up to one billion unknowns, for both Riemannian gradient descent and Riemannian conjugate gradient methods, whose practical performance is also related to the Hessian condition number. The Thomas--Fermi flow needs the fewest iterations, while the metrics inverted exactly by tensor-product solvers are the fastest in computational time on one GPU card.
tldr: The paper analyzes Riemannian Hessian condition numbers for Sobolev gradient flows solving the Gross-Pitaevskii ground state problem, proposing new metrics and showing improved convergence in numerical tests.
motivation: Sobolev gradient flows are effective for computing Gross-Pitaevskii ground states, but their convergence behavior across different metrics lacks a uniform theoretical understanding.
method: The authors derive bounds on the Rayleigh quotient of the Riemannian Hessian at the ground state, providing a uniform convergence analysis for classical and new metrics, including a Thomas-Fermi metric.
result: The analysis yields condition-number bounds, proves uniform boundedness for the Thomas-Fermi metric in 1D harmonic traps, and numerical tests up to one billion unknowns confirm the predicted iteration counts and performance.
conclusion: The Riemannian Hessian framework gives practical guidance for choosing metrics in Sobolev gradient flows, with the Thomas-Fermi metric requiring the fewest iterations and tensor-product-solvable metrics being fastest on GPU.

title: Formalisation Of Information Processing And Intelligence In Proteinoid Networks
authors: Panagiotis Mougkogiannis Andrew Adamatzky
abstract: ArXiv:2610.13545v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Proteinoid microspheres are electrically active assemblies of thermally polymerised amino acids that exhibit spontaneous oscillations, spike-like events, stimulus-dependent responses, adaptation and collective dynamics. We formulate these observations as an applied-mathematical problem and develop a unified dynamical framework for information processing in proteinoid networks. Individual microspheres are represented by nonlinear excitable or oscillatory systems, whereas interactions are described by weighted adaptive graphs and, in the spatial limit, reaction--diffusion dynamics. The framework combines signal propagation, attenuation, fading memory, adaptive coupling, synchronisation, information transfer, reservoir readout, robustness and energetic constraints. We define a task-relative proteinoid intelligence functional from normalised measures of stimulus information, memory, adaptation, directed information transfer, task performance and robustness, penalised by energetic and structural costs. Analytical results establish a joint-response information bound, an upper bound on linear memory for stable linear networks, and existence of an optimal admissible coupling matrix under compact constraints. Dimensionless groups identify the relative time scales and coupling regimes governing the problem in nonlinear and adaptive network dynamics.
tldr: The paper develops a unified dynamical framework for information processing and intelligence in proteinoid microsphere networks, incorporating signal propagation, memory, adaptation, and energetic constraints.
motivation: Proteinoid microspheres exhibit complex electrical dynamics such as oscillations, spike-like events, and collective behavior, motivating a formal mathematical treatment of their information processing capabilities.
method: Individual microspheres are modeled as nonlinear excitable or oscillatory systems, with interactions described by weighted adaptive graphs and reaction-diffusion dynamics; a task-relative intelligence functional is defined using normalized measures of stimulus information, memory, adaptation, directed information transfer, task performance, and robustness, penalized by energetic and structural costs.
result: Analytical results include a joint-response information bound, an upper bound on linear memory for stable linear networks, and the existence of an optimal admissible coupling matrix under compact constraints; dimensionless groups identify relative time scales and coupling regimes.
conclusion: The framework provides a formal basis for quantifying intelligence and information processing in proteinoid networks, though it remains outside the quantum information and thermodynamics directions of the researcher's interests.

title: Neural Polar Codes For Source Coding
authors: Bashar Huleihel, Ziv Aharoni, Haim H. Permuter
abstract: ArXiv:2610.13554v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper presents a data-driven approach to lossless and lossy source compression using polar codes. Classical polar source coding achieves fundamental limits with low complexity for binary memoryless sources. However, for unknown q-ary sources with memory, successive-cancellation (SC) decoding requires an explicit source model and can be computationally prohibitive. We present analytical SC recursions and show that exact implementations scale quadratically with alphabet size and cubically with state-space size. To overcome these limitations, we develop neural polar decoders trained directly from data to approximate conditional distributions of synthetic polar coordinates without requiring an explicit source model. These learned distributions enable estimation of entropy rates, mutual information, and rate-distortion functions, and support explicit polar compression schemes. For lossless compression, we identify high-entropy polarized coordinates and reconstruct the remaining coordinates using the learned SC recursion. For lossy compression, we combine neural polar decoders with a neural test channel to estimate and optimize the mutual information-distortion tradeoff and construct an explicit lossy polar code. We also extend the framework to Wyner-Ziv compression with decoder side information by learning conditional polarized distributions and a reconstruction mapping. Experiments on memoryless sources, sources with memory, and real genomic data show that the learned decoders closely match analytical SC decoders when available and remain applicable when conventional methods are computationally infeasible or the source model is unavailable.
tldr: Presents neural polar decoders for lossless and lossy source coding, including Wyner-Ziv compression, that learn conditional distributions from data without explicit source models.
motivation: Classical polar source coding requires an explicit source model and becomes computationally prohibitive for unknown q-ary sources with memory, motivating data-driven alternatives.
method: Develops analytical successive-cancellation recursions and neural polar decoders trained to approximate conditional distributions of synthetic polar coordinates, combined with a neural test channel for lossy compression and a reconstruction mapping for Wyner-Ziv coding.
result: Experiments on memoryless, memoryful, and real genomic sources show the learned decoders closely match analytical SC decoders when available and remain applicable when conventional methods are infeasible or source models are unknown.
conclusion: Neural polar codes extend polar source coding to model-free settings and enable estimation of entropy rates, mutual information, and rate-distortion functions, but the work is purely classical and does not address quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: On Privacy Mechanism Design Under A Bounded $\alpha$-Lift Leakage Constraint With $\chi^2$-Utility
authors: Amirreza Zamani, Mohammad Amin Zarrabian, Parastoo Sadeghi, Mikael Skoglund
abstract: ArXiv:2610.13685v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the design of a statistical privacy mechanism under a bounded [MATH]-lift leakage constraint. An agent observes useful data [MATH], which is arbitrarily correlated with private data [MATH], and releases [MATH]. The goal is to maximize Pearson [MATH]-information [MATH] while satisfying the point-wise privacy constraint. This utility is an [MATH]-information that is nonnegative, obeys data processing, and measures the aggregate normalized change from the prior [MATH] to the posteriors [MATH]. The main benefit of this choice is that [MATH] is exactly quadratic in the posterior perturbations; hence, no local approximation of the utility is required. For the nonlinear [MATH]-lift constraint, we derive a uniform Taylor-remainder bound that remains valid for the optimizing, [MATH]-dependent perturbation. When [MATH] is invertible, this yields a closed-form quadratic surrogate, an explicitly scaled binary mechanism that satisfies the original [MATH]-lift constraint, a computable sufficient range for [MATH], and an [MATH] bound on the utility gap. For [MATH], the solution is exact over an explicit range. We transfer these results to point-wise R\'enyi-divergence privacy, including an exact-feasible mechanism, an explicit privacy-budget range, and matching gap bounds. We also give an exact formulation for arbitrary leakage matrices and evaluate exact-feasible mechanisms numerically.
tldr: The paper designs a statistical privacy mechanism under a bounded alpha-lift leakage constraint, maximizing chi^2-information utility, with closed-form solutions for invertible leakage matrices and extensions to Rényi-divergence privacy.
motivation: Privacy mechanism design often requires balancing utility and leakage, and existing methods may need local approximations or lack exact bounds for nonlinear constraints.
method: They derive a uniform Taylor-remainder bound for the nonlinear alpha-lift constraint, yielding a closed-form quadratic surrogate and an explicitly scaled binary mechanism that satisfies the original constraint.
result: For invertible leakage matrices they provide exact feasible mechanisms, a computable sufficient range for alpha, and an O(·) bound on the utility gap; for alpha=1 the solution is exact over an explicit range; results transfer to point-wise Rényi-divergence privacy with exact-feasible mechanisms and matching gap bounds.
conclusion: The approach offers computable privacy guarantees with quadratic utility, but it is a purely classical information-theoretic privacy result with no direct connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid systems, so it falls outside the user's research directions.

title: Quantum-like Architecture Of The Social Atom: Mental Marker Coherence And The Triple-Resonance Mechanism Of Cognitive Activation
authors: Andrei Khrennikov, Christian Aspalter, Likan Zhan
abstract: ArXiv:2610.12472v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Social Laser Theory (SLT) provides a rigorous quantum-like mathematical formalism for modeling collective social activation. While its macroscopic effects mimic laser physics, the fundamental driver of the lasing regime resides in the internal state dynamics of the social atom. In this paper, we propose a quantum-like architecture for the individual cognitive system, formalizing the social atom as a composite quantum system where mental markers - spanning cognitive, affective, and valence dimensions - are represented as internal degrees of freedom in a complex Hilbert space. We show that social activation is not a classical linear response but is governed by a Triple-Resonance Mechanism: the simultaneous quantum-like matching of semantic topic, energetic impact, and valence stance between the agent's internal state and the informational field. We detail how the repeated processing of quantized informational units (infons) leads to a state of cognitive population inversion. We further establish a link to Human Entanglement Theory (HET), suggesting that the emergence of coherent informational fields is rooted in the phase alignment of these internal mental markers across a population. By situating SLT within the broader framework of Social Quantum Field Theory (SQFT), this paper provides a neuro-cognitive foundation for collective phenomena such as emotional contagion and rapid narrative amplification. Our results suggest that the Social Laser is a macroscopic manifestation of quantum-like effects across the human cognitive and neuro-social architecture.
tldr: The paper proposes a quantum-like cognitive architecture for the social atom, with mental markers as internal degrees of freedom and a triple-resonance mechanism driving social activation.
motivation: Social Laser Theory mimics laser physics macroscopically, but the internal driver of lasing in the social atom remains unclear; this work aims to formalize the individual cognitive system underlying collective activation.
method: The authors model mental markers across cognitive, affective, and valence dimensions as internal states in a complex Hilbert space, and define a triple-resonance condition for matching semantic topic, energetic impact, and valence stance with an informational field.
result: Repeated processing of quantized informational units (infons) leads to cognitive population inversion, and phase alignment of mental markers across a population links to Human Entanglement Theory and coherent informational fields.
conclusion: The Social Laser is interpreted as a macroscopic manifestation of quantum-like effects in human cognitive and neuro-social architecture, providing a foundation for emotional contagion and narrative amplification.

title: Topologically Steerable Ultra-flat Electro-optic Combs Via non-Hermitian Frequency Lattices
authors: Weiwei Liu, Xiaolong Su, Bing Wang, Yongjie Wang, Pang Fu, Wenxian Zhang, Ruiqian Cheng, Songpan Hong, Qingbin Zhang, Peixiang Lu
abstract: ArXiv:2610.12867v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Electro-optic (EO) frequency combs convert microwave signals to the optical domain with deterministic repetition rates, enabling applications in optical telecommunications, microwave photonics, and LiDAR. However, generating flat EO combs has remained a long-standing challenge due to exponential decay of the spectral envelope inherent to bidirectional frequency coupling within conventional schemes. Here we reveal the inherent correspondence between flat-comb generation and the topological energy bands of non-Hermitian nonreciprocal frequency lattices, and experimentally realize ultra-flat combs with topologically controlled spectral flow. We derive the exact analytical condition for flat-comb generation, and find that it maps precisely onto the complex energy band, thereby establishing a direct connection between comb-envelope engineering and non-Hermitian topology. Experimentally, we observe an ultra-flat comb whose frequency evolution direction is governed by the topological winding and remains robust against detuning and phase fluctuations. This scheme can be further extended to long-range coupling and multi-lattice architectures, underscoring its versatility for flat dual- and multi-comb generation. Our work establishes a topologically steerable approach for achieving ultra-flat EO combs, paving the way for chip-scale spectral engineering via non-Hermitian topology.
tldr: The paper demonstrates ultra-flat electro-optic frequency combs by mapping flat-comb generation onto the topological energy bands of non-Hermitian nonreciprocal frequency lattices.
motivation: Flat electro-optic frequency combs are difficult to generate because conventional bidirectional frequency coupling leads to exponential spectral envelope decay.
method: The authors derive an exact analytical condition for flat-comb generation and show it corresponds to the complex energy band of a non-Hermitian frequency lattice, then experimentally realize topologically controlled spectral flow.
result: They observe an ultra-flat comb whose frequency evolution direction is set by the topological winding and is robust against detuning and phase fluctuations.
conclusion: This establishes a topologically steerable approach for ultra-flat EO combs, enabling chip-scale spectral engineering via non-Hermitian topology.

title: Classification Of Bipartite Observables Ii: Nip Observables And The Todorcevic Trichotomy
authors: Jos\'e Iovino Eduardo Due\~nez
abstract: ArXiv:2610.12908v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A bipartite observable is stable when its idealized responses are continuous. We show that it is NIP exactly when they are of the first Baire class. They then form a Rosenthal compactum, and the dividing lines of Shelah in model theory, together with the classification of Rosenthal compacta of Todorevi\'c, acquire a physical meaning. For observables, mixtures of states make every hereditarily separable compactum of idealized responses metrizable, and the Todorevi\'c trichotomy becomes a classification into three classes. Each class contains a physical order: the comparison of photon numbers, the comparison of positions, and the causal order of spacetime, whose idealized responses are not first countable because a light cone can shrink to a point; the comparison of two phases on a circle joins it there. Each of the seven minimal families of the heptachotomy, which Argyros, Dodos and Kanellopoulos extracted from the methods of Todorevi\'c, is realized by a tree of preparations of photons, of a particle in a box, or of a spin chain read by a probe; the spin chain also shows that NIP, unlike its uniform version, is not symmetric between the two parties. Finally, for the Ising model in a transverse field we show that, in the ordered phase, the responses of the two pure phases form split pairs whose midpoints, the responses of the symmetric state, form an uncountable discrete set; the proof uses a Lee--Yang theorem for this model.
tldr: The paper uses model theory and topology to classify bipartite observables, showing that stable observables correspond to continuous responses and NIP observables to first Baire class responses, with physical interpretations via Todorcevic's trichotomy.
motivation: To give physical meaning to Shelah's model-theoretic dividing lines and Todorcevic's classification of Rosenthal compacta through the lens of quantum observables.
method: Applies model-theoretic notions (stability, NIP), topology of Rosenthal compacta, and physical examples including photon number, position, causal order, spin chains, and the transverse-field Ising model.
result: NIP observables yield Rosenthal compacta and metrizability under state mixtures; the Todorcevic trichotomy becomes a three-class physical classification, the seven minimal families of the heptachotomy are realized by quantum preparations, and the Ising ordered phase produces an uncountable discrete set of symmetric-state responses.
conclusion: The work provides a mathematical classification of bipartite observables with physical interpretations, linking model theory and topology to quantum observables, but it lies outside the four main research directions.

title: Haar Measure For Totally Positive Split Real Semisimple Quantum Groups Of Classical Type
authors: Kenny de Commer, Geoffrey Janssens, Wannes Malfait
abstract: ArXiv:2610.13213v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let [MATH] be a non-zero real number and put [MATH]. Let [MATH] be a semisimple split real Lie group of classical type, with Lie algebra [MATH] and associated Borel subalgebra [MATH]. We show that there exists a locally compact quantum group [MATH] which integrates the Borel part [MATH] of the Drinfeld--Jimbo quantized enveloping algebra [MATH], viewed as a Hopf [MATH]-algebra. We further compute the associated Haar weights and modular data for [MATH]. Up to an excess Cartan part, the Drinfeld double of [MATH] can be seen as an analytic quantization of the function algebra of the totally positive semigroup [MATH].
tldr: Constructs a locally compact quantum group integrating the Borel part of the Drinfeld–Jimbo quantized enveloping algebra and computes its Haar weights and modular data.
motivation: The paper aims to provide an analytic quantization of the function algebra of the totally positive semigroup via the Drinfeld double of the Borel part of quantum groups.
method: Uses the theory of locally compact quantum groups, Drinfeld–Jimbo quantized enveloping algebras, and Borel subalgebras for split real semisimple Lie groups of classical type.
result: It shows existence of such a quantum group, computes its Haar weights and modular data, and relates its Drinfeld double to an analytic quantization of the totally positive semigroup up to an excess Cartan part.
conclusion: The work advances the analytic theory of quantum groups and totally positive structures but is outside the listed quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, and hybrid systems directions.

title: Secrets In Preamble: Practical And Robust Phy Information Hiding For Wi-Fi
authors: Rui Pan, Guanxiong Shen, Linning Peng, Xinyu Qi, Junqing Zhang
abstract: ArXiv:2610.13367v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Physical layer (PHY) information hiding refers to the concealment of secrets within PHY waveforms without compromising the integrity of the primary communication link, thereby enabling critical applications such as covert communication, PHY steganography, and watermarking. The widespread deployment of Wi-Fi has motivated substantial research interest in hiding secrets within Wi-Fi waveforms. However, existing Wi-Fi information hiding approaches suffer from two limitations: restricted steganographic capacity and insufficient robustness against environmental variations, both of which severely constrain practical deployment. This work proposes to embed secrets within the Wi-Fi legacy short training field (L-STF). The designed method preserves the autocorrelation properties of Wi-Fi L-STF, ensuring that packet detection and coarse frequency offset compensation functionalities remain uncompromised. The secret embedding and extraction processes employ a pair of neural networks designed to learn optimal embedding rules and maximize steganographic capacity. We developed a prototype system and conducted comprehensive experiments across both indoor and outdoor environments. Experimental results show that our method can reliably embed 46 secret bits within Wi-Fi packets across diverse channel conditions, achieving significantly enhanced steganographic capacity and environmental robustness. The hardware prototype study validates the feasibility of the proposed Wi-Fi information hiding scheme.
tldr: A neural-network-based physical-layer information hiding scheme embeds secrets into the Wi-Fi L-STF field, achieving 46 hidden bits per packet with improved robustness across indoor and outdoor channels.
motivation: Existing Wi-Fi PHY information hiding approaches suffer from limited steganographic capacity and poor robustness against environmental variations, hindering practical deployment.
method: Secrets are embedded within the Wi-Fi legacy short training field (L-STF) while preserving its autocorrelation properties, with a pair of neural networks trained to learn optimal embedding and extraction rules.
result: A hardware prototype reliably embeds 46 secret bits per Wi-Fi packet across diverse indoor and outdoor channel conditions, demonstrating significantly enhanced capacity and robustness.
conclusion: The work validates the feasibility of practical, robust Wi-Fi PHY-layer information hiding for covert communication and watermarking applications.

title: Coherent Ultraviolet Frequency Combs Generated By Resonant Dispersive Waves
authors: Michael Hemsworth, Arthur K. Mills, Christina Hofer, TJ Hammond, David J. Jones
abstract: ArXiv:2610.12620v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Resonant dispersive wave (RDW) emission in gas-filled anti-resonant hollow-core fibers (AR-HCF) offers a wavelength-tunable route to ultraviolet (UV) and vacuum ultraviolet (VUV) frequency comb generation. RDW emission is expected to be coherent fundamentally, but various noise sources are expected to limit the coherence, including amplitude-to-phase fluctuations due to input pulse intensity noise and plasma formation. It is critical, therefore, to establish the limits of the coherence of UV RDW pulses to determine their applicability for precision spectroscopy. Here, we demonstrate the coherence of RDW emission at 260~nm generated with an amplified Yb-doped fiber system at a 2-MHz repetition rate with a self-heterodyne beat measurement between the RDW and the fourth harmonic of the source. We isolate the RDW contribution to the frequency noise by coherently subtracting the carrier-envelope offset noise contribution measured simultaneously with an f-2f interferometer. We observe a beatnote linewidth below 10~kHz over timescales longer than 100~ms, and we find a conservative upper bound of 1~rad on the integrated RMS phase deviations over a frequency range spanning 1 to 30~kHz. The dominant frequency noise contributions are consistent with environmental noise of the interferometers and AR-HCF coupling fluctuations. These results provide strong evidence that RDW emission is coherent under well-controlled experimental conditions, confirming its potential for UV and VUV frequency comb generation.
tldr: The paper demonstrates that resonant dispersive wave emission in gas-filled anti-resonant hollow-core fibers can generate coherent ultraviolet frequency combs at 260 nm with beatnote linewidth below 10 kHz.
motivation: Ultraviolet and vacuum ultraviolet frequency combs are valuable for precision spectroscopy, but the coherence of resonant dispersive wave emission must be established to assess its applicability.
method: The authors use an amplified Yb-doped fiber system at a 2-MHz repetition rate and perform a self-heterodyne beat measurement between the RDW at 260 nm and the fourth harmonic of the source, while subtracting carrier-envelope offset noise via an f-2f interferometer.
result: They observe a beatnote linewidth below 10 kHz over timescales longer than 100 ms and set a conservative upper bound of 1 rad on the integrated RMS phase deviations from 1 to 30 kHz, with dominant noise attributed to environmental and fiber-coupling fluctuations.
conclusion: These results provide strong evidence that RDW emission is coherent under controlled conditions, supporting its potential for UV and VUV frequency comb generation for precision spectroscopy.

title: Entropic-ordered Superfluid
authors: Andrew Lucas Isabella Zane
abstract: ArXiv:2610.12635v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present a minimal classical lattice model of superfluidity at arbitrarily high temperatures, using a modified three-dimensional XY model with ``soft" rotors. The global U(1) symmetry is spontaneously broken above a positive critical temperature due to entropic order. We study hydrodynamics in this high-temperature regime and verify consistency with the fluctuation-dissipation theorem, explaining how the large noise variance at very high temperatures is not sufficient to destroy superfluidity or the long lifetime of Goldstone modes.
tldr: A classical 3D XY model with soft rotors exhibits spontaneous U(1) symmetry breaking and superfluidity at arbitrarily high temperatures due to entropic order.
motivation: To understand whether superfluidity can survive at high temperatures and how large thermal noise affects Goldstone modes and hydrodynamics.
method: A minimal classical lattice model of superfluidity is introduced using a modified three-dimensional XY model with soft rotors; hydrodynamics in the high-temperature regime is analyzed and checked against the fluctuation-dissipation theorem.
result: The model shows spontaneous breaking of global U(1) symmetry above a positive critical temperature via entropic order, and the large noise variance at high temperatures does not destroy superfluidity or the long lifetime of Goldstone modes.
conclusion: Entropic order provides a mechanism for high-temperature superfluidity in a classical lattice model, with hydrodynamic consistency and robust Goldstone modes.

title: Percolation Of Data Constraints And Reorganization Of Boolean Function States In Parity Learning
authors: Han Ma
abstract: ArXiv:2610.13233v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study how a neural network reorganizes its learned function as training proceeds and as previously unseen parity data accumulate. The trained model is itself a Boolean function on binary strings of finite length. We then evaluate it on all data, inside and outside the training set, and read off its complete sign table. Its [MATH] entries are the amplitudes of a normalized state, dubbed the function-state, whose inverse subsystem purity [MATH] is an effective Schmidt rank. We find that small data additions broaden the Schmidt spectrum, whereas larger additions reconcentrate it in the target mode. The former is called differentiation because the model distinguishes inputs more sharply. The latter is called target-selective recoherence, where the model settles on the single rule shared by the added data. As the dataset grows, the connectivity of the constraint graph defined by the training set increases monotonically, whereas the learned inverse purity changes nonmonotonically. On a fixed connected dataset, as learning proceeds, the Schmidt spectrum begins to reorganize, followed by gains in target alignment and later by improvement in predictive accuracy. This ordering distinguishes three aspects of learning: constraint identifiability, function-state organization, and predictive accuracy. At fixed data size, a function that has already been learned can re-differentiate, an event we call retreat, without changing graph connectivity. Recovery reconcentrates the Schmidt spectrum in a similar target-selective pattern, without exact recurrence of the Boolean state. Thus the percolation of data constraints fixes the identifiable support, while the reduced state produced by training continues to reorganize even after that support stops changing.
tldr: The paper uses a quantum-inspired function-state representation to analyze how neural networks learn parity functions, showing that data constraint percolation fixes identifiable support while the learned Boolean function state reorganizes nonmonotonically.
motivation: To understand how neural networks reorganize learned Boolean functions during training and as previously unseen parity data accumulate, beyond merely tracking predictive accuracy.
method: A neural network is trained on parity data, then evaluated on all binary inputs to obtain its complete sign table, which is mapped to a normalized function-state whose inverse subsystem purity serves as an effective Schmidt rank; constraint graph connectivity and Schmidt spectrum dynamics are analyzed.
result: Small data additions broaden the Schmidt spectrum (differentiation), whereas larger additions reconcentrate it in the target mode (target-selective recoherence); graph connectivity increases monotonically while learned inverse purity changes nonmonotonically, and Schmidt spectrum reorganization precedes gains in target alignment and accuracy.
conclusion: The percolation of data constraints determines the identifiable support, but the reduced state produced by training continues to reorganize even after that support stops changing, distinguishing constraint identifiability, function-state organization, and predictive accuracy.

title: Linear And Entropy-stable Scheme For The Dynamic Van Der Waals Model Of Non-isothermal Liquid-vapor Flows
authors: Yunzhuo Guo, Zhonghua Qiao, Xianmin Xu
abstract: ArXiv:2610.13029v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we propose a linear and decoupled fully discrete scheme that preserves the entropy production property for the dynamic van der Waals model. This model provides a thermodynamically consistent diffuse-interface framework for describing non-isothermal phase transitions in single-component liquid-vapor systems, containing the coupled conservation laws of mass, momentum and energy. We first introduce an equivalent reformulation of the governing equations that avoids the use of chain-rule identities, which generally fail under discrete differentiation. Further, a component-wise convex-splitting method is employed to calculate the discrete chemical potential and temperature. This treatment provides a discrete entropy-stable inequality without a time step restriction. Based on the explicitly treated velocity, the scheme allows the three conservation equations to be solved linearly and sequentially in a decoupled manner. Since the momentum equation does not directly affect the entropy-stability analysis, we use a classical linear semi-implicit scheme to solve it. Numerical experiments verify the expected numerical accuracy. Simulations of droplet evaporation and two- and three-dimensional Leidenfrost effects further demonstrate the proposed method can capture complex non-isothermal phase-transition dynamics while numerically reproducing the discrete entropy production behavior.
tldr: A linear, decoupled, fully discrete entropy-stable scheme is proposed for the dynamic van der Waals model of non-isothermal liquid-vapor flows.
motivation: The dynamic van der Waals model is a thermodynamically consistent diffuse-interface framework for non-isothermal phase transitions, but designing efficient numerical schemes that preserve entropy production is challenging.
method: The authors reformulate the governing equations to avoid chain-rule identities, use component-wise convex splitting for chemical potential and temperature, and solve the coupled conservation laws linearly and sequentially in a decoupled manner.
result: Numerical experiments verify accuracy, and simulations of droplet evaporation and 2D/3D Leidenfrost effects reproduce complex non-isothermal phase-transition dynamics while obeying a discrete entropy production inequality.
conclusion: The proposed scheme is linear, decoupled, and entropy-stable without time-step restrictions, making it effective for simulating non-isothermal liquid-vapor flows.

title: Structure-Aware Online Optimization Of The Age Of Information With Unknown System Statistics
authors: Yoshiaki Inoue, Michel Mandjes, Liron Ravner
abstract: ArXiv:2610.13142v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Timely information dissemination is essential in modern communication systems, where low informational latency is critical for networked control, monitoring, and real-time decision-making. The Age of Information (AoI) has emerged as a fundamental metric for quantifying information freshness at the receiver. A key challenge in AoI optimization is selecting the update generation rate: infrequent updates lead to stale information, whereas overly frequent updates increase queueing delays. We develop a structure-aware, data-driven framework for adaptive AoI optimization modeled as single-server queues with unknown system statistics. Our key idea is to exploit analytical representations of the AoI gradient, which depend on a finite-dimensional collection of system quantities that can be estimated from observations collected during system operation. This reduces the online learning problem to estimating the quantities required by the gradient, rather than learning the AoI objective as a black box. We propose an online stochastic approximation algorithm that jointly estimates these quantities and optimizes the update generation rate. We prove almost sure convergence of the algorithm to the optimal update generation rate under mild regularity and moment conditions, despite the temporal dependence induced by the underlying queueing process. We demonstrate the framework in four representative incomplete-information settings, including FCFS queues with unknown service characteristics or hidden background traffic, a preemptive LCFS system with partial observations, and a generate-at-will system with threshold waiting.
tldr: This paper develops a structure-aware online stochastic approximation framework for optimizing the Age of Information in single-server queueing systems with unknown statistics.
motivation: Timely information dissemination is critical in communication networks, and the Age of Information quantifies freshness, but choosing the update generation rate requires knowing system statistics that are often unknown.
method: The authors exploit analytical gradient representations of AoI and reduce the online learning problem to estimating finite-dimensional system quantities, then propose an online stochastic approximation algorithm for joint estimation and optimization.
result: They prove almost sure convergence to the optimal update generation rate under mild regularity and moment conditions, demonstrating the framework in four incomplete-information queueing settings.
conclusion: The proposed data-driven approach provides a provably convergent solution for adaptive AoI optimization without prior system statistics, applicable to various queueing disciplines.

title: On Surjective Max-Phase Isometries Of Schatten p-Classes (0<p<1)
authors: Qi Liu Wenwen Zhang
abstract: ArXiv:2610.13271v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate max-phase isometries on Schatten quasi-classes in the range [MATH]. Motivated by the rigidity theory for smooth normed spaces [ (2025), Article 126], we establish its operator-theoretic counterpart in the quasi-Banach setting. We prove that every surjective max-phase isometry on a finite-dimensional Schatten class is a standard real-linear Schatten isometry multiplied by an even sign-valued function, without any continuity assumption. This extends the scope of the classical Schatten isometry classification [ (1994), 239--242] to nonlinear mappings preserving only unsigned two-point metric data. Our approach combines support orthogonality, a symmetrized rank-one spectral formula, and a max-profile uniqueness principle. For arbitrary Hilbert spaces, we obtain the corresponding classification on finite-rank operators, while continuity yields the full-space result. We also establish preservation of rank, singular values, and two-sided support orthogonality.
tldr: The paper classifies surjective max-phase isometries on finite-dimensional Schatten quasi-classes for 0<p<1, extending classical Schatten isometry results to nonlinear mappings preserving unsigned two-point metric data.
motivation: Motivated by rigidity theory for smooth normed spaces, the authors seek an operator-theoretic analogue in the quasi-Banach setting of Schatten p-classes with p<1.
method: They combine support orthogonality, a symmetrized rank-one spectral formula, and a max-profile uniqueness principle to prove classification without continuity assumptions.
result: Every surjective max-phase isometry on a finite-dimensional Schatten class is a standard real-linear Schatten isometry multiplied by an even sign-valued function; for arbitrary Hilbert spaces, finite-rank operators are classified, and continuity yields the full-space result.
conclusion: The work extends Schatten isometry classification to nonlinear max-phase isometries and also establishes preservation of rank, singular values, and two-sided support orthogonality.

title: Sample-Preserving Search-to-Decision Reduction For Noisy Linear Equations Over Large Moduli
authors: Andrej Bogdanov, Kel Zin Tan, Prashant Nalini Vasudevan
abstract: ArXiv:2610.12913v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Noisy Linear Equations problem involves finding the solution to a random linear system over a finite field given noisy evaluations. This is a generalisation of various learning problems widely used in cryptography, including Learning with Errors (LWE), Learning with Rounding (LWR), and Learning Parity with Noise (LPN). We present a new sample-preserving search-to-decision reduction for Noisy Linear Equations that has complexity [MATH], where [MATH] is the dimension of the secret, [MATH] is the number of samples, [MATH] is the modulus, and [MATH] is the magnitude of the noise (defined suitably for the kind of noise involved). In particular, this implies search-to-decision reductions for LWE and LWR that run in time [MATH] even if the modulus [MATH] is exponentially large, as long as the noise-to-modulus ratio [MATH] is non-negligible. Our reduction works for prime moduli [MATH]. If [MATH] is composite, it instead produces a list that contains a small multiple of the solution. Prior to this work, known search-to-decision reductions for LWE and LWR either did not preserve the parameters of the problem (i.e., [MATH], [MATH], [MATH], and [MATH]), or had complexity that scaled polynomially with either [MATH] or the largest prime factor of [MATH].
tldr: The paper presents a new sample-preserving search-to-decision reduction for Noisy Linear Equations, with implications for LWE and LWR over large moduli.
motivation: Search-to-decision reductions are central to the foundations of learning-with-errors-style cryptographic problems, but prior reductions for LWE and LWR either lost parameter preservation or scaled poorly with the modulus or its prime factors.
method: The authors construct a sample-preserving reduction for Noisy Linear Equations over prime moduli with complexity depending on dimension, sample count, modulus, and noise magnitude, and extend it to composite moduli by outputting a list containing a small multiple of the solution.
result: The reduction yields search-to-decision reductions for LWE and LWR that run in time polynomial in the dimension and sample count even when the modulus is exponentially large, provided the noise-to-modulus ratio is non-negligible.
conclusion: This work advances the classical cryptographic theory of noisy linear equations and LWE/LWR reductions, but it is not directly connected to the quantum information, thermodynamics, networking, or hybrid systems directions.

title: Goal-Oriented Ordered Autoencoding For Successive Refinement In Progressive Communication
authors: Dario Bega Qi Liao
abstract: ArXiv:2610.13426v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Goal-oriented communication often struggles to sustain downstream task performance under variable and unpredictable bandwidth. We address this problem by proposing GO-OAE (Goal-Oriented Ordered AutoEncoding), which learns a progressively refinable quantized latent sequence, optimized directly for task utility rather than source reconstruction. Each component of the sequence is represented for transmission by its code index, and the learned ordering enables inference from any received prefix of the index sequence, with performance improving as more indices arrive. We prove that optimizing the goal-oriented distortion objective is equivalent to solving a weighted conditional information bottleneck formulation, and introduce an unbiased multi-prefix importance sampling (MPIS) estimator, to reduce GO-OAE training computational cost from O(BK) to O(Bm) with m << K, and reduces the estimator variance by a factor of 1/m. Experiments show that, on MiniImageNet, GO-OAE achieves over 96% of the lossless upper-bound classification accuracy using 324 bits per image (683X compression vs. raw RGB), and already attains over 94% of the upper bound with only 70% of the transmitted indices. It consistently outperforms reconstruction-optimized codecs and ordered autoencoders trained with uniform prefix sampling across all transmission budgets, demonstrating effective communication at extreme compression rates.
tldr: GO-OAE learns a progressively refinable quantized latent sequence optimized for task utility, enabling goal-oriented communication under variable bandwidth via ordered autoencoding and multi-prefix importance sampling.
motivation: Goal-oriented communication often struggles to sustain downstream task performance under variable and unpredictable bandwidth, motivating a progressive transmission method that prioritizes task utility over reconstruction.
method: The paper proposes Goal-Oriented Ordered AutoEncoding (GO-OAE), which represents each latent component by a code index and enables inference from any received prefix. It proves equivalence to a weighted conditional information bottleneck and introduces an unbiased multi-prefix importance sampling (MPIS) estimator to reduce training cost from O(BK) to O(Bm) and variance by 1/m.
result: On MiniImageNet, GO-OAE achieves over 96% of lossless upper-bound classification accuracy using 324 bits per image (683X compression), and over 94% with only 70% of indices transmitted. It outperforms reconstruction-optimized codecs and ordered autoencoders trained with uniform prefix sampling.
conclusion: GO-OAE demonstrates effective extreme-compression progressive communication by directly optimizing task utility, with theoretical connections to information bottleneck and efficient training via MPIS.

title: Phantom Zernike Wavefront Sensor: Phase Contrast With Engineered Focal Plane Reference Speckles
authors: Benjamin Courtney-Barrer
abstract: ArXiv:2610.12807v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce the Phantom Zernike Wavefront Sensor (phantom ZWFS), an engineered reference extension of phase-contrast wavefront sensing in which controlled pupil plane modulation generates off-axis coherent speckle structures that undergo localized focal plane phase shifts. These references may replace the central ZWFS reference when the on-axis PSF core is required for another optical function, such as photonic science coupling, or may augment a conventional central ZWFS response to provide additional wavefront information. Using a monochromatic scalar model, we derive the resulting carrier structure and show how the engineered references can be recovered through spatial demodulation and incorporated into calibrated reconstruction. A simple four-reference realization demonstrates that the reference geometry redistributes photon sensitivity across spatial frequency magnitude and orientation, producing mode dependent changes in linearity and cross-talk rather than a uniform improvement over a classical ZWFS. We then consider differential piston on a seven segment aperture as an application specific example. A hybrid sensor retaining the central ZWFS phase region and adding six engineered references that match the segment geometry gives similar precision near the phased state but substantially improved performance at larger piston excursions. Under the adopted photon-noise-limited benchmark, the hybrid reduces the nonlinear reconstruction error and provides better conditioned optical encoding of the piston state than an idealized vector ZWFS, allowing more precise piston estimation from the same detected photon flux at larger piston excursions.
tldr: The paper introduces the Phantom Zernike Wavefront Sensor, an engineered phase-contrast wavefront sensing scheme that uses off-axis focal-plane reference speckles to redistribute photon sensitivity and improve piston estimation over a seven-segment aperture.
motivation: Conventional Zernike wavefront sensors consume the on-axis PSF core with a central phase reference, which is problematic when that core is needed for other optical functions such as photonic science coupling; a reference scheme that avoids this constraint is therefore desirable.
method: Using a monochromatic scalar diffraction model, the authors derive the carrier structure produced by controlled pupil-plane modulation, recover the engineered references via spatial demodulation, and compare a four-reference realization and a hybrid sensor (central phase region plus six segment-matched references) against an idealized vector Zernike WFS.
result: The reference geometry redistributes photon sensitivity across spatial frequency magnitude and orientation, yielding mode-dependent changes in linearity and cross-talk rather than uniform improvement; the hybrid sensor achieves similar precision near the phased state and substantially better performance at larger piston excursions under a photon-noise-limited benchmark.
conclusion: Engineered off-axis reference speckles can augment or replace the central Zernike reference, providing better-conditioned optical encoding of the piston state and enabling more precise piston estimation from the same photon flux at large excursions.

title: All-electron Rt-tddft With Exact Exchange Based On Numeric Atom-centered Orbitals For Condensed Matter
authors: Jianhang Xu, Christopher Shepard, Yosuke Kanai
abstract: ArXiv:2610.12896v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Real-time time-dependent density functional theory (RT-TDDFT) has become a widely used first-principles method for studying excited-state and nonequilibrium electron dynamics. Hybrid exchange-correlation (XC) functionals, which incorporate a fraction of nonlocal exact exchange, are particularly important for accurately describing processes such as charge transfer and hot-carrier dynamics. However, the high computational cost which accompanies exact exchange, as required in hybrid XC functionals, has largely restricted RT-TDDFT simulations of condensed matter systems to using semi-local XC functionals. In this work, we present an all-electron implementation of exact exchange for RT-TDDFT based on numeric atom-centered orbitals, extending an efficient ground-state resolution-of-identity (RI) framework to the complex, time-dependent Hamiltonians required for real-time propagation. We validate the implementation against an established RI approach, for an isolated water molecule, finding exact agreement for both valence and core (K-edge) excitations. We also demonstrate the method on two extended periodic systems, crystalline silicon and silicon carbide. For silicon, the HSE06 spectrum reproduces previously reported real-time TDDFT results and agrees with experiment to within approximately 0.2~eV, consistent with plane-wave pseudopotential implementations. For silicon carbide, we compute valence and X-ray absorption spectra at the silicon [MATH]-edge and carbon [MATH]-edge. These results establish an efficient, all-electron route to hybrid-XC functional RT-TDDFT for both molecular and condensed matter systems.
tldr: The paper presents an all-electron real-time time-dependent density functional theory implementation with exact exchange using numeric atom-centered orbitals for condensed matter systems.
motivation: Hybrid exchange-correlation functionals with exact exchange are important for accurately describing charge transfer and hot-carrier dynamics, but their high computational cost has restricted RT-TDDFT simulations of condensed matter to semi-local functionals.
method: The authors extend an efficient ground-state resolution-of-identity framework to the complex, time-dependent Hamiltonians required for real-time propagation, enabling all-electron exact exchange in RT-TDDFT.
result: They validate the implementation against an established RI approach for a water molecule and demonstrate it on crystalline silicon and silicon carbide, computing valence and X-ray absorption spectra.
conclusion: The work establishes an efficient all-electron route to hybrid-XC functional RT-TDDFT for both molecular and condensed matter systems.

title: Alter-excitons In Altermagnets: Symmetry, Splitting And Dispersion
authors: Yuanfan Xiong, Liangyu Wang, Xuan Wu, Wei Hu, Jinlong Yang
abstract: ArXiv:2610.12900v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Magnetism provides a fertile platform for discovering emergent quantum phenomena governed by symmetry. Recent developments of spin-space-group (SSG) theory have revealed altermagnets as a distinct class of nonrelativistic collinear magnets with unconventional spin-dependent electronic structures. Here, we demonstrate that altermagnetic symmetry imposes fundamentally different constraints on electronic and excitonic excitations. Although the quasiparticle and two-body Hamiltonians possess identical SSG symmetries, we find that symmetry-protected degeneracies present in the electronic band structure can be intrinsically lifted in the exciton spectrum at specific momenta. This splitting arises solely from the many-body nature of excitons and does not require spin-orbit coupling or noncollinear magnetic order. Combining symmetry analysis with many-body perturbation theory, we predict a novel class of spin-split excitonic quasiparticles, termed alter-excitons, and reveal their characteristic dispersions in altermagnetic systems. Our results establish excitons as a sensitive probe of hidden spin-space symmetries and uncover a new route toward symmetry-engineered many-body phenomena in collinear magnets.
tldr: The paper predicts a new class of spin-split excitonic quasiparticles, termed alter-excitons, in altermagnetic systems using symmetry analysis and many-body perturbation theory.
motivation: Altermagnets exhibit unconventional spin-dependent electronic structures, and the authors aim to understand whether and how altermagnetic symmetry affects excitonic excitations beyond single-particle band structures.
method: They combine spin-space-group symmetry analysis with many-body perturbation theory to compare electronic and excitonic Hamiltonians and compute exciton spectra and dispersions.
result: They find that symmetry-protected degeneracies in the electronic band structure can be intrinsically lifted in the exciton spectrum at specific momenta, producing spin-split excitonic quasiparticles without spin-orbit coupling or noncollinear magnetic order.
conclusion: Excitons are proposed as sensitive probes of hidden spin-space symmetries, opening a route to symmetry-engineered many-body phenomena in collinear magnets.

title: Silent Breakdown Of The Perturbative Polarization Expansion In The Terahertz Regime
authors: Yao Lu, Jiawei Zhang, Qiang Wu, Jingjun Xu
abstract: ArXiv:2610.12982v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Nonlinear optics expands the polarization in powers of the drive and retains only the lowest-order terms. This truncation is safe at optical frequencies, where the convergence field lies far above the damage threshold. In the terahertz regime, phonon polaritons enhance the nonlinear susceptibilities by orders of magnitude, lowering the convergence field into the sub-damage range and opening a window in which the expansion fails while the crystal remains recoverable. We term this window silent breakdown. At resonance, the nearest singularities of the driven lattice mode are a complex-conjugate pair of branch points below the multistability threshold, so the response remains smooth and single-valued even though the [MATH] description fails. The convergence field scales as [MATH], so sharpening a resonance enhances the nonlinearity but narrows the range over which the expansion applies. It follows from the mode shift [MATH] alone, [MATH], giving 2[MATH]9 MV/cm for [MATH]. Since resonant enhancement is central to terahertz nonlinear optics, this boundary defines the field range over which susceptibility-based descriptions are quantitatively reliable.
tldr: The paper identifies a 'silent breakdown' window in the terahertz regime where the perturbative polarization expansion of nonlinear optics fails due to phonon-polariton enhancement, even though the crystal response remains smooth and recoverable.
motivation: Nonlinear optics conventionally truncates the polarization expansion at lowest order, which is safe at optical frequencies because the convergence field exceeds the damage threshold. The authors ask whether this assumption survives in the terahertz regime, where resonant phonon-polariton enhancement can push the convergence field into a sub-damage range.
method: The authors analyze the driven lattice mode near resonance and locate the nearest singularities of the response in the complex field plane, showing they form a complex-conjugate pair of branch points located below the multistability threshold, and derive how the convergence field scales with resonance sharpness and mode shift.
result: The expansion fails within a finite field window while the crystal remains recoverable, a phenomenon termed 'silent breakdown'; the convergence field scales as predicted from the mode shift, giving roughly 2-9 MV/cm for the considered parameters and showing that sharpening a resonance both enhances nonlinearity and narrows the validity range of the expansion.
conclusion: Resonant enhancement in terahertz nonlinear optics defines a hard boundary on the field range over which susceptibility-based descriptions are quantitatively reliable, which must be accounted for in high-field terahertz experiments and device design.

title: Matrix-free Numerical Continuation Of The Ikeda Map In Passive Kerr Resonators
authors: Yuandi Xu, Pengxiang Wang, Jianxing Pan, Haisu Zhang, Gang Xu
abstract: ArXiv:2610.12994v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce a matrix-free numerical continuation framework for the Ikeda map of coherently driven passive Kerr resonators. The framework traces solution branches and evaluates their linear stability without explicitly assembling the full Jacobian matrices, using a unified formulation for states that recur after one or multiple round trips. We resolve stable and unstable branches of modulation-instability patterns and temporal cavity solitons, and uncover period-doubled homogeneous states and associated multi-round-trip dynamics that are absent from the standard Lugiato-Lefever equation (LLE). For period-1 states, the Ikeda map and the LLE show close agreement in the high-finesse regime, while their branch-existence intervals increasingly deviate as the finesse decreases. These results demonstrate that direct continuation of the unaveraged round-trip map can capture nonlinear states and multi-round-trip dynamics beyond the mean-field description, providing a systematic framework for bifurcation and stability analysis of Kerr resonators without relying on the averaged LLE.
tldr: The paper introduces a matrix-free numerical continuation framework for the Ikeda map of passive Kerr resonators and compares it with the Lugiato-Lefever equation.
motivation: Passive Kerr resonators exhibit rich nonlinear dynamics, but standard mean-field models like the Lugiato-Lefever equation may miss multi-round-trip physics and period-doubled states.
method: A matrix-free continuation algorithm traces solution branches and evaluates linear stability of the Ikeda map without explicitly assembling full Jacobian matrices, using a unified formulation for states recurring after one or multiple round trips.
result: The framework resolves stable and unstable branches of modulation-instability patterns and temporal cavity solitons, reveals period-doubled homogeneous states and associated multi-round-trip dynamics absent from the Lugiato-Lefever equation, and quantifies deviation between the Ikeda map and the Lugiato-Lefever equation as finesse decreases.
conclusion: Direct continuation of the unaveraged round-trip map provides a systematic bifurcation and stability analysis of Kerr resonators beyond the averaged Lugiato-Lefever description.

title: Quaternion Gaussian Probes For Tensor Frobenius-Norm Estimation
authors: Yannan Chen, Hailin Sun, Min Xi
abstract: ArXiv:2610.12534v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large-scale tensors arising in science and engineering are often too large to form or store explicitly. Their multilinear contractions, however, can frequently be evaluated efficiently, which makes randomized Frobenius-norm estimation a practical alternative to exact computation. In this paper, we study estimation of the squared Frobenius norm of a real order-[MATH] tensor from such contractions using independent real, complex, or quaternion Gaussian probes. For a rank-one tensor, one normalized sample is a product of [MATH] independent Gamma variables. This gives exact relative-variance factors [MATH], [MATH], and [MATH], respectively. Under the same budget of underlying real Gaussian vectors, the quaternion probe has smaller rank-one variance than four independent real probes for [MATH]; a real-channel representation identifies the gain as modewise pooling. For orthogonal CP tensors, the exact relative variance equals the corresponding rank-one factor divided by the participation-ratio effective rank and the number of samples. For arbitrary real tensors, we prove sharp uniform moment bounds, attained at rank one, and obtain Chebyshev guarantees. A classical block-median construction then gives two-sided exponential confidence for the modified estimator. Numerical examples test the rank-one and effective-rank formulas. An implicit infinite-series kernel tensor illustrates contraction-based norm evaluation; EEG maps provide a qualitative spatial interpolation illustration.
tldr: The paper studies randomized estimation of the squared Frobenius norm of large real tensors using real, complex, or quaternion Gaussian probes and multilinear contractions.
motivation: Large-scale tensors are often too large to store explicitly, but their contractions can be evaluated efficiently, making randomized norm estimation a practical alternative to exact computation.
method: The authors derive exact relative-variance factors for rank-one tensors under real, complex, and quaternion Gaussian probes, then extend the analysis to orthogonal CP tensors and arbitrary real tensors via moment bounds.
result: Quaternion probes can have smaller rank-one variance than four independent real probes under the same real-Gaussian budget, and sharp uniform moment bounds plus Chebyshev and exponential confidence guarantees are obtained.
