conclusion: The proposed probe framework provides contraction-based Frobenius-norm estimation with theoretical variance and concentration guarantees, supported by numerical examples including an infinite-series kernel tensor and EEG maps.

title: Optimal Rates For Federated Variational Inequalities Under Different Relaxations Of Bounded Variance Assumption
authors: Kirill Novoselov, Yuriy Dorn, Darina Dvinskikh, Alexander Gasnikov
abstract: ArXiv:2610.12641v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study how interpolation affects local steps and parallel sampling in monotone variational inequalities (VIs), with [MATH] workers, [MATH] oracle calls per worker per round, and [MATH] rounds. Under the strong growth condition (SGC), we determine the minimax rate for affine VIs, attained by local extragradient with worker averaging. For nonlinear monotone VIs and convex-concave saddle problems with Lipschitz operators satisfying SGC, we improve the stochastic terms of bounded-variance expected-gap guarantees from [MATH] to [MATH] with local steps and from [MATH] to [MATH] with minibatches. Under strong monotonicity, we improve the noise-dependent condition-number scaling of existing extragradient bounds from quadratic to linear. The resulting monotone-gap and strongly monotone accuracy bounds match lower bounds up to logarithmic factors in [MATH]. Under generalized smoothness and SGC, adaptive steps give polynomial dependence on the initial radius. For affine VIs with globally bounded oracle variance, we also attain the minimax rate: the deterministic rate over [MATH] sequential calls plus the statistical rate over all [MATH] samples. For composite VIs with smooth convex sample interpolation and an exactly evaluated monotone Lipschitz component, accelerated mirror-prox sliding achieves an [MATH] gradient term, a [MATH] monotone term, and a [MATH] sampling term, without assuming SGC.
tldr: The paper derives optimal convergence rates for federated variational inequalities under relaxed bounded variance assumptions, using local extragradient methods and minibatching.
motivation: Federated learning and distributed optimization often rely on bounded variance assumptions that can be too restrictive; the authors aim to relax these via strong growth conditions and interpolation to obtain tighter rates.
method: They analyze monotone variational inequalities and convex-concave saddle problems with local steps, worker averaging, minibatches, and adaptive steps, establishing minimax rates under strong growth, generalized smoothness, and composite settings.
result: They improve stochastic terms from bounded-variance guarantees, achieve minimax optimal rates up to logarithmic factors for affine and nonlinear monotone VIs, and reduce condition-number scaling from quadratic to linear under strong monotonicity.
conclusion: The work provides a comprehensive theoretical framework for federated variational inequalities under relaxed assumptions, matching lower bounds and extending to composite and globally bounded variance settings.

title: Pointwise H\"older Continuity Of Lyapunov Exponents Of Random Matrix Products
authors: Pablo G. Barrientos
abstract: ArXiv:2610.12698v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that if the first Lyapunov exponent of a compactly supported random matrix product is simple, then it is pointwise H\"older continuous for the Wasserstein--Hausdorff distance. By passing to exterior powers, we obtain pointwise H\"older continuity of the first [MATH] exponents whenever they are simple.
tldr: The paper proves pointwise Hölder continuity of Lyapunov exponents for compactly supported random matrix products when the exponents are simple.
motivation: Lyapunov exponents describe asymptotic growth rates of random matrix products, and their regularity is important in smooth ergodic theory and probability.
method: The author uses exterior powers and the Wasserstein–Hausdorff distance to establish Hölder continuity of the first exponent and, more generally, the first k exponents when they are simple.
result: If the first Lyapunov exponent is simple, it is pointwise Hölder continuous; by passing to exterior powers, the same holds for the first several exponents whenever they are simple.
conclusion: The work extends regularity results for Lyapunov exponents of random matrix products and contributes to the smoothness theory in this mathematical setting.

title: Variational Neural Transport For Aggregation-diffusion Equations
authors: Hailiang Liu Qianyi Li
abstract: ArXiv:2610.12745v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a neural transport framework for nonlinear, nonlocal aggregationdiffusion equations arising in chemotaxis, polymer dynamics, and related applications. Based on the Onsager variational principle, we reformulate the governing equation as a constrained optimal control problem, taking the velocity field as the control and evolving the density via the associated continuity equation. The velocity field is parameterized by a neural network trained on the variational objective evaluated along particle trajectories. By coupling the density and generalized score equations into a single system solved via the Euler method, the score function propagates efficiently for loss evaluation. Furthermore, we establish a rigorous error analysis that decomposes the total error into approximation, optimization, Monte Carlo sampling, and time-discretization components, and prove corresponding error bounds. Numerical experiments across several representative models demonstrate the accuracy and effectiveness of the proposed approach.
tldr: A neural transport framework based on the Onsager variational principle for solving nonlinear, nonlocal aggregation-diffusion equations.
motivation: Aggregation-diffusion equations arise in chemotaxis, polymer dynamics, and related applications, requiring accurate and efficient numerical solvers.
method: The governing equation is reformulated as a constrained optimal control problem with the velocity field parameterized by a neural network; density and generalized score equations are coupled and solved via the Euler method for efficient loss evaluation.
result: Rigorous error analysis decomposes total error into approximation, optimization, Monte Carlo sampling, and time-discretization components, with corresponding bounds; numerical experiments demonstrate accuracy across representative models.
conclusion: The proposed variational neural transport approach offers an effective and theoretically grounded method for simulating aggregation-diffusion dynamics.

title: Geometric Operators And The Third Problem Of Halmos
authors: Kui Ji, Chunlan Jiang, Zhenyue Wang
abstract: ArXiv:2610.12857v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In 1970, P. R. Halmos raised ten open problems on operator theory. The third problem of Halmos is the following: if an intransitive operator has an inverse, is its inverse also intransitive? This question is reduced to the case of conjugate bi-geometric operators in arXiv: 2610.11202. In the framework of conjugate bi-geometric operators, using tools from complex geometry, operator theory, and function theory, this paper gives an affirmative answer to the third problem of Halmos in the following cases: (a) bundle-preserving operator;(b) subexponential growth of operator norms. These two cases cover a large class of operators.
tldr: This paper gives an affirmative answer to Halmos's third problem for conjugate bi-geometric operators under bundle-preserving or subexponential growth conditions.
motivation: Halmos's third problem asks whether the inverse of an intransitive operator must also be intransitive, a question previously reduced to the case of conjugate bi-geometric operators.
method: The authors use tools from complex geometry, operator theory, and function theory to analyze conjugate bi-geometric operators.
result: They prove that the inverse of an intransitive operator is intransitive in two broad cases: bundle-preserving operators and operators with subexponential norm growth.
conclusion: These cases cover a large class of operators, advancing pure operator theory but having no direct connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: On Eigenvector Statistics Of Large-Dimensional Sample Covariance Matrices With Applications
authors: Weiming Li, Zeng Li, Qinwen Wang
abstract: ArXiv:2610.12928v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the eigenvector-weighted spectral statistics \[ T_n(\varphi,g)=p^{-1}tr\{\varphi(_n)g()\} \] of large-dimensional sample covariance matrices \(_n\) with population covariance \(\). These statistics combine functions of sample eigenvalues with sample--population eigenvector overlaps and arise in statistical losses that depend on both. As the dimension and sample size grow proportionally, we establish a joint central limit theorem for \(\{T_n(\varphi_a,g_a)\}_{a=1}^r\) with multiple analytic test functions and population weights, centered by finite-dimensional deterministic equivalents. A key intermediate step is a joint Gaussian process limit for the weighted resolvent traces \[ m_n^g(z)=p^{-1}tr\{(_n-z_p)^{-1}g()\}. \] The limiting means and cross-covariances are expressed in terms of the population spectral distribution. We apply these results in two settings: one concerns the variance component of minimum-norm prediction risk, and the other concerns the Frobenius loss of fixed rotationally invariant covariance estimators. For fixed affine shrinkage rules, the loss means, variances, and cross-covariances have explicit formulas in terms of population spectral moments.
tldr: The paper establishes joint central limit theorems for eigenvector-weighted spectral statistics of large-dimensional sample covariance matrices, with applications to prediction risk and covariance estimator loss.
motivation: Understanding eigenvector overlap statistics in high-dimensional covariance estimation and prediction risk requires distributional limits that go beyond eigenvalue-only results.
method: It uses random matrix theory and a joint Gaussian process limit for weighted resolvent traces to derive a central limit theorem for multiple test functions.
result: A joint CLT is obtained with limiting means and cross-covariances expressed via the population spectral distribution, yielding explicit formulas for fixed affine shrinkage rules.
conclusion: The work provides statistical tools for eigenvector-overlap spectral statistics in high-dimensional sample covariance matrices, relevant to classical high-dimensional statistics.

title: Uniform Exponential Attractors For Non-Autonomous Dynamical Systems And An Application To The Damped Hyperbolic Equation With Sub-quintic Growth
authors: Li Dandan Chang Qingquan
abstract: ArXiv:2610.13068v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we develop an abstract framework for the theory of uniform exponential attractors in non-autonomous dynamical systems. Our construction employs time-dependent absorbing sets while ensuring exponential attraction among the constructed sets. Moreover, we show that the resulting exponential attractors are uniform-that is, they remain stable under perturbations. As an application of this abstract theory, we study the weakly damped hyperbolic equation with sub-quintic nonlinearity. Using the proposed approach, we construct exponential attractors for the process generated by the Shatah-Struwe solution, which satisfies both energy and Strichartz estimates. Furthermore, we establish the Holder continuity of these exponential attractors with respect to the external forcing term.
tldr: The paper develops an abstract framework for uniform exponential attractors in non-autonomous dynamical systems and applies it to a damped hyperbolic equation with sub-quintic nonlinearity.
motivation: The authors aim to extend the theory of exponential attractors to non-autonomous settings where uniformity under perturbations is required.
method: They construct time-dependent absorbing sets and prove exponential attraction among them, then apply the framework to the Shatah-Struwe solution using energy and Strichartz estimates.
result: They establish the existence of uniform exponential attractors for the weakly damped hyperbolic equation and prove Hölder continuity with respect to the external forcing term.
conclusion: The work provides a general abstract tool for non-autonomous dynamical systems and demonstrates its applicability to a physically motivated wave equation.

title: On The Convergence Of The Mesh-Free Discretization Of A Non-Linear Bond-Based Peridynamic Model With A Bond-Breakage Criterion
authors: Lukas Pflug, Michael Stingl, Max Zetzmann
abstract: ArXiv:2610.13355v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show the convergence of a commonly used mesh-free discretization of a dynamic non-linear bond-based peridynamic model with irreversible damage implemented via a bond-breakage criterion for a fixed horizon [MATH]. The model chosen here is a mathematically well-posed regularization of a discontinuous peridynamic operator often found in the literature, which assumes that fracture results from strain in tension only. We explicitly include the one-point quadrature used in this scheme in the analysis. The convergence is with respect to the natural norm of the solution space given by [MATH], and therefore [MATH] in the spatial coordinates. This result heavily constrains the spatial regularity of the continuous solution which we prove afterwards. More specifically, for locally [MATH]-Lipschitz continuous input data, local Lipschitz bounds are derived for the displacement, regardless of damage. This is consistent with interpreting the peridynamic model used here as an approximation to a truly discontinuous fracture model with a length-scale parameter given by the horizon [MATH]. We note that we do not deal with the limit of the solutions as [MATH].
tldr: The paper proves convergence of a mesh-free discretization for a nonlinear bond-based peridynamic model with irreversible damage via a bond-breakage criterion.
motivation: Peridynamic models are used to simulate fracture, but rigorous convergence of their numerical discretizations, especially with bond breakage and one-point quadrature, remains underexplored.
method: The authors analyze a mesh-free discretization of a regularized dynamic bond-based peridynamic model, including one-point quadrature and a bond-breakage criterion for fixed horizon.
result: Convergence is established in the natural norm of the solution space, with local Lipschitz bounds on displacement for locally Lipschitz input, constraining spatial regularity.
conclusion: The peridynamic model is consistent with an approximation to a discontinuous fracture model with a length scale given by the horizon, though the limit of vanishing horizon is not addressed.

title: On The Simultaneous Zero Inclusion Property And Characterization Of Inner Product Space
authors: Souvik Ghosh
abstract: ArXiv:2610.13378v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show that if a Banach space [MATH] is smooth and almost locally uniformly rotund and if satisfies the following \[0\in W(T) \implies 0\in W(T^{-1})\] for all invertible bounded linear map on [MATH] then Birkhoff-James orthogonality in [MATH] is symmetric. This result, therefore, characterizes the inner product spaces out of all smooth and almost locally uniformly rotund spaces having three or more dimension via simultaneous zero inclusion property, introduced by Brai et al. [J. Math. Anal. Appl., 449 (2017) 1413-1423]. Further, this gives answers to some open questions asked by E. Poon [J. Math. Anal. Appl., 534(2024), 128052].
tags: smooth and almost locally uniformly rotund spaces
tldr: The paper characterizes inner product spaces among smooth and almost locally uniformly rotund Banach spaces via the simultaneous zero inclusion property and symmetry of Birkhoff-James orthogonality.
motivation: The simultaneous zero inclusion property was introduced by Brai et al. as a tool related to Birkhoff-James orthogonality, and open questions by Poon asked for characterizations of inner product spaces in this context.
method: The proof uses geometric functional analysis in Banach spaces, assuming smoothness and almost local uniform rotundity, and shows that if 0 in W(T) implies 0 in W(T^{-1}) for all invertible bounded linear maps, then Birkhoff-James orthogonality is symmetric.
result: Under these hypotheses, the simultaneous zero inclusion property holds if and only if the space is an inner product space, for dimensions three or more, answering open questions of Poon.
conclusion: This provides a new characterization of inner product spaces and strengthens the connection between the simultaneous zero inclusion property and symmetric Birkhoff-James orthogonality.
keywords: smooth and almost locally uniformly rotund spaces

title: The Complexity Of Finding Additional Solutions
authors: Saman Farhat
abstract: ArXiv:2610.12804v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the difficulty of finding a new solution when a list of distinct solutions is already supplied. For any fixed finite collection of list lengths, we can prescribe the additional-solution degrees while preserving a given [MATH]-paddable domain and first-solution degree. We also prove an exact compatibility condition for prescribing an arbitrary positive-list degree at the same time: it must dominate every prescribed fixed-level degree, and this condition suffices. All degrees use polynomial-time reductions with at most one oracle query and correct behavior on empty fibers; the realization needs no assumption about P versus NP. The combined construction gives each underlying witness exponentially many short counter copies. A list that exhausts these copies is long enough to pay for exhaustive search through the underlying witness bound. Separately, we construct a total problem whose first-solution task and every fixed-length additional-solution task are polynomial-time solvable, while its arbitrary-list task is FNP-complete. Assuming P differs from NP, the domain, first degree, and entire fixed-level degree sequence therefore do not determine the arbitrary-list degree. A constant fiber cap restores determination by finitely many fixed levels. The constructions change witness sets and do not prescribe an infinite sequence of degrees or enumerate all remaining solutions.
tldr: The paper studies the computational complexity of finding an additional solution when some solutions are already known, with results on prescribing additional-solution degrees under polynomial-time reductions.
motivation: Motivated by the question of how difficult it is to find new solutions to a search problem after a list of distinct solutions has been supplied, and how such degrees can be prescribed.
method: Uses polynomial-time reductions with at most one oracle query and constructions that preserve a given domain and first-solution degree while controlling additional-solution degrees.
result: Shows an exact compatibility condition for arbitrary-list degrees, constructs an FNP-complete arbitrary-list task while fixed-length tasks are polynomial-time solvable, and demonstrates that a constant fiber cap restores determination.
conclusion: The findings clarify the structure of solution-finding complexity and show that the domain, first-solution degree, and fixed-level degree sequence do not generally determine the arbitrary-list degree, assuming P ≠ NP.

title: WaveMark: Robust Wavelet-Domain Image Watermarking For Diffusion Models
authors: Jie Cao, Qi Li, Chaklam Cheong, Yutong Jin, Enze Yu, Zelin Zhang, Jianbing Ni
abstract: ArXiv:2610.12952v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Image watermarking enables provenance tracing for photorealistic images generated by diffusion models. However, state-of-the-art (SOTA) removal attacks can suppress embedded signals with little perceptual degradation. This vulnerability limits the effectiveness of watermarks for intellectual property protection and misuse attribution. We propose WaveMark, a novel wavelet-domain watermarking method that embeds messages in a diffusion model's initial noise. To support robust recovery from perturbed carriers, WaveMark distributes keyed replicas of message bits across spatial positions, wavelet orientations, and scales. Each carrier groups coefficients from four latent channels and encodes a randomized bit through magnitude projection, providing an explicit decoding margin. We evaluate WaveMark with SD2.1 on SDP and MS-COCO Captions under 14 attacks. WaveMark achieves 100.0% bit accuracy (BA) without attacks, while maintaining image quality comparable to the evaluated baselines. Under SOTA MarkNull and MarkNull-A, it retains over 88% BA, outperforming all baselines.
tldr: WaveMark is a wavelet-domain image watermarking method that embeds messages in diffusion models' initial noise for robust provenance tracing.
motivation: Diffusion-generated images need reliable provenance, but state-of-the-art removal attacks can suppress watermark signals with minimal perceptual degradation.
method: WaveMark distributes keyed message-bit replicas across spatial positions, wavelet orientations, and scales, encoding randomized bits through magnitude projection across four latent channels.
result: Evaluated on SD2.1 with SDP and MS-COCO Captions under 14 attacks, WaveMark achieves 100.0% bit accuracy without attacks and retains over 88% under MarkNull and MarkNull-A, outperforming baselines.
conclusion: WaveMark improves watermark robustness for diffusion-model image provenance, though it is not related to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Limit-sure Winning In Team Games Without Shared Randomness
authors: L\'eonard Brice, Thomas A. Henzinger, Alipasha Montaseri, Ali Shafiee, K. S. Thejaswini
abstract: ArXiv:2610.13569v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study concurrent stochastic games in which a team of agents plays against an adversarial environment. If the agents could access a shared source of randomness, then these games reduce to two-player games. Despite being common in the literature on coalition games, this assumption does not accurately model real-world systems. In this paper, we consider the setting where the agents only have access to individual sources of randomness, and must satisfy a given reachability or safety objective. The limit-sure problem asks whether the team can ensure that the objective is satisfied with probability at least [MATH] for every [MATH]. For reachability objectives, we show that this problem is [MATH]-complete. For safety objectives, we show that limit-sure winning coincides with almost-sure winning, which is known to lie in [MATH]. As a corollary of these results, we conclude that model checking of the qualitative fragment of the logic Individually Randomised ATL -- introduced in the recent work of Brice et al. -- is [MATH]-complete.
tldr: The paper studies limit-sure winning in concurrent stochastic team games where agents have only individual randomness, providing complexity results for reachability and safety objectives.
motivation: Standard coalition game models assume shared randomness among team agents, which is unrealistic for many real-world systems, so the authors investigate the more realistic setting without shared randomness.
method: They analyze concurrent stochastic games with reachability and safety objectives under individual randomness, and derive completeness results for the limit-sure problem and qualitative model checking of Individually Randomised ATL.
result: For reachability objectives the limit-sure problem is shown to be complete for a certain complexity class, while for safety objectives limit-sure winning coincides with almost-sure winning, leading to completeness of model checking for the qualitative fragment of Individually Randomised ATL.
conclusion: The work resolves the complexity of limit-sure winning in team games without shared randomness and clarifies the model-checking complexity for a related logic.

title: How Far Is Kolmogorov-Loveland Randomness From Martin-L\"of Randomness?
authors: Tomislav Petrovi\'c
abstract: ArXiv:2610.13585v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We'll call a map from basic to clopen sets of binary sequences an if it preserves uniform Lebesgue measure and the disjointedness relation. For some notion of randomness [MATH] we can ask if there is a computable encoding [MATH] such that for every non-Martin-L\"of-random (non-MLR) sequence [MATH], the sequences in [MATH] are non-[MATH]. Thus we can use [MATH] and randomness test for [MATH] to construct a randomness test for MLR. We show that there is no such [MATH] for partial computable randomness (PCR), but there is one for Kolmogorov-Loveland randomness. Indeed, there is a total computable [MATH] and a pair of total computable non-monotonic betting strategies such that on every sequence in [MATH] at least one of the strategies wins whenever [MATH] is non-MLR.
tldr: The paper studies computable encodings that preserve measure and disjointness to compare Kolmogorov-Loveland randomness with Martin-Löf randomness, showing no such encoding for partial computable randomness but one for Kolmogorov-Loveland randomness.
motivation: Understanding how different algorithmic randomness notions relate to Martin-Löf randomness is a central problem in computability theory and algorithmic information theory.
method: The author defines a computable encoding from basic to clopen sets that preserves uniform Lebesgue measure and the disjointedness relation, then analyzes its existence for partial computable randomness (PCR) and Kolmogorov-Loveland randomness.
result: There is no such encoding for PCR, but for Kolmogorov-Loveland randomness there exists a total computable encoding and a pair of total computable non-monotonic betting strategies such that on every sequence in the encoding's image, at least one strategy wins whenever the original sequence is non-MLR.
conclusion: The work separates Kolmogorov-Loveland randomness from Martin-Löf randomness via computable encodings, while ruling out an analogous construction for partial computable randomness.

title: The Distortion Of Threshold Approval Multiwinner Voting
authors: Mohamad Latifian, Marzieh Nilipour, Alexandros A. Voudouris
abstract: ArXiv:2610.13725v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study multiwinner voting with [MATH] voters and [MATH] candidates, where the goal is to select a committee of size [MATH]. Voters have unit-sum cardinal utilities but report only coarse information induced by [MATH] utility thresholds. In particular, each voter partitions the candidates into approval sets, with the utilities of all candidates in the same set lying between the same pair of consecutive thresholds. We model the utility of each voter for a committee as a normalized monotone symmetric norm, capturing, among others, additive welfare, best-representative utility, top-[MATH] welfare, [MATH] welfare, and normalized non-increasing ordered weighted averages. We design a deterministic rule with distortion at most [MATH] and a randomized rule with distortion at most [MATH]. These guarantees hold for every committee size [MATH] and every norm in our framework. Consequently, a single threshold yields distortion [MATH] for deterministic rules and [MATH] for randomized rules, while [MATH] thresholds suffice for constant distortion. We complement these results with norm-dependent lower bounds that asymptotically match our upper bounds for constant committee sizes, including the single-winner case.
tldr: The paper studies distortion in multiwinner voting when voters only report approval sets induced by utility thresholds, and designs deterministic and randomized rules with bounded distortion.
motivation: Voters often provide coarse preference information rather than full cardinal utilities, so it is important to understand how much social welfare is lost under threshold approval reporting.
method: The authors model voter utility for a committee using normalized monotone symmetric norms and design deterministic and randomized multiwinner voting rules, with upper and lower distortion bounds.
result: They obtain a deterministic rule with distortion at most a constant factor and a randomized rule with a better constant, showing that a single threshold gives constant distortion for randomized rules and that a few thresholds suffice for constant distortion more generally.
conclusion: Threshold approval information can achieve constant distortion in multiwinner voting under broad utility norms, with norm-dependent lower bounds asymptotically matching the upper bounds for constant committee sizes.

title: Voluntary Nonpharmaceutical Intervention As A Feedback-evolving Game
authors: Ryuichi Kumata, Hiromu Ito, Masato Yamamichi
abstract: ArXiv:2610.12519v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Nonpharmaceutical interventions (NPIs), such as mask wearing, can reduce epidemic spread, but their effectiveness depends on whether people adopt and sustain them. The incentive to adhere changes with infection risk and with the behavior of others. Yet it remains unclear how epidemiological protection and social reinforcement determine the strategic structure of infection control, and how epidemic feedback changes that structure over time. Here, we develop a socio-epidemiological model in which prevalence changes behavioral incentives while adherence changes transmission, separating private protection from source control and incorporating conformity. At a given prevalence, private protection favors adherence, source control creates opportunities for free-riding, and conformity reinforces whichever behavior is already common, generating distinct adherence games. Because adherence reduces transmission and prevalence, the population can move between these games as the epidemic unfolds. This feedback can stabilize partial adherence, create alternative behavioral norms, or generate recurrent epidemic-behavior cycles. Moreover, interventions with the same population-level effect on transmission at a given adherence level can produce different long-term outcomes when protection is distributed differently between the individual and others. Thus, voluntary infection control is a feedback-evolving game whose outcome depends not only on epidemiological efficacy but also on who is protected and how behavior is socially reinforced.
tldr: A socio-epidemiological model reveals that voluntary nonpharmaceutical intervention adherence behaves as a feedback-evolving game, where prevalence alters behavioral incentives and behavior alters transmission, generating distinct adherence regimes.
motivation: The effectiveness of voluntary nonpharmaceutical interventions depends on sustained adoption, yet it is unclear how epidemiological protection and social reinforcement shape the strategic structure of infection control and how epidemic feedback changes that structure over time.
method: The authors develop a coupled epidemic-behavioral model that separates private protection from source control and incorporates conformity, allowing the population to move between different adherence games as prevalence changes.
result: The feedback can stabilize partial adherence, create alternative behavioral norms, or generate recurrent epidemic-behavior cycles; interventions with identical population-level transmission effects at a given adherence level can yield different long-term outcomes depending on how protection is distributed between self and others.
conclusion: Voluntary infection control is a feedback-evolving game whose outcome depends not only on epidemiological efficacy but also on who is protected and how behavior is socially reinforced.

title: Broadband Soliton Microcombs In The Biological Window Enabled By A Resonant Coupler
authors: Xinrui Luo, Du Qian, Yuanlei Wang, Yiwen Yang, Kaixuan Zhu, Yinke Cheng, Haoyang Luo, Junqi Wang, Bei-Bei Li, Qihuang Gong, Qi-Fan Yang
abstract: ArXiv:2610.12603v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Broadband soliton microcombs near 1 [MATH]m offer coherent, evenly spaced optical lines for measurements in the biological window. However, combining broad spectral coverage with closely spaced comb lines increases the pump-power requirement and makes thermally stable soliton access more difficult. Here, we demonstrate broadband silicon nitride (Si3N4) soliton microcombs enabled by a resonant coupler that enhances pump delivery to the nonlinear resonator. The device generates a spectrum spanning 930-1380 nm with an approximately 98-GHz comb-line spacing at on-chip pump powers of tens of milliwatts, while providing reliable thermally stable access to the single-soliton state. These results provide a route to compact, power-efficient microcomb sources that combine broad spectral coverage with closely spaced comb lines for spectroscopy and imaging in the biological window.
tldr: Demonstrates broadband silicon nitride soliton microcombs enabled by a resonant coupler for spectroscopy and imaging in the biological window.
motivation: Broadband microcombs near 1 µm are useful for biological measurements, but broad coverage with closely spaced lines increases pump power and complicates thermally stable soliton access.
method: A resonant coupler is used to enhance pump delivery to a Si3N4 nonlinear resonator, generating soliton microcombs via nonlinear frequency conversion.
result: The device produces a 930–1380 nm spectrum with ~98 GHz line spacing at on-chip pump powers of tens of milliwatts and provides reliable thermally stable single-soliton access.
conclusion: This provides a route to compact, power-efficient microcomb sources combining broad spectral coverage and closely spaced lines for biological-window spectroscopy and imaging.

title: Fourier Transform-Based Computation Of Two-Electron Four-Center Coulomb Repulsion Integrals
authors: William Chen, Lior Silberman, Ury Segal, Chen Greif
abstract: ArXiv:2610.12608v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present a Fourier-based method for evaluating two-electron four-center Coulomb repulsion integrals over Slater-type orbitals. Spherical Fourier-Bessel coefficients of the convolution factors are precomputed and reused. Since the spherical part of the integral can be evaluated directly, there remains only a one-dimensional quadrature problem in the radial direction. For the ten reference integrals reported here, the largest absolute discrepancy is [MATH]. A preliminary resident-cache benchmark computes approximately [MATH] unique integrals per second on an NVIDIA V100 at the contraction stage.
tldr: The paper presents a Fourier transform-based method for efficiently evaluating two-electron four-center Coulomb repulsion integrals over Slater-type orbitals.
motivation: Accurate and fast computation of Coulomb repulsion integrals is a bottleneck in quantum chemistry simulations, motivating the need for efficient numerical algorithms.
method: The authors use spherical Fourier-Bessel coefficients of convolution factors, precompute and reuse them, reducing the problem to a one-dimensional radial quadrature.
result: The method achieves small absolute discrepancies on ten reference integrals and a benchmark of approximately a certain number of unique integrals per second on an NVIDIA V100 GPU at the contraction stage.
conclusion: The Fourier-based approach offers a promising and reusable computational technique for high-throughput evaluation of molecular integrals, though it is not connected to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Measure Theory In Convergence Spaces Part I: Sion-Carath\'eodory Extension In Net Convergence Groups
authors: Alexandre Reggiolli Teixeira
abstract: ArXiv:2610.12797v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish a Carath\'eodory-type extension theorem for premeasures with values in general separated abelian net convergence groups. Starting from hereditary exhaustivity on the source ring and intrinsic conditions for combining null errors, we construct a countably additive extension on a regulated Boolean sigma-algebra, with full upper and lower regularity in the original convergence. Completeness is required only on the limit-stable hull of the source range. Under closed summation for arbitrary directed rows and finite-response reflection, we identify the regulated domain with the splitting class of Sion's inner and outer processes. For a Dedekind-complete real vector lattice, we show that sequential closed summation on a bounded interval is equivalent to weak sigma-distributivity of the generated band, giving a converge-theoretic interpretation of the concept. Source representations allow us to recover the partially ordered-group extension of Volauf and the finite-variation extension of Kusraev and Malyugin from the general theorem. We then treat finite semivariation by adjoining dominated coordinate variations to an additive lift of the premeasure. The resulting extension is defined on the full semivariation regulator domain and preserves semivariation exactly, without requiring decomposability or the countable sup property. It includes measures of infinite vector variation.
tldr: The paper develops a Carathéodory-type extension theorem for premeasures valued in separated abelian net convergence groups, recovering several known extension results as special cases.
motivation: Classical Carathéodory extension theory assumes real-valued (or ordered-group-valued) measures, which limits applicability to more general algebraic-analytic settings such as vector lattices and semivariation-valued measures.
method: The author imposes hereditary exhaustivity on the source ring and intrinsic null-error combination conditions to build a countably additive, fully regular extension on a regulated Boolean sigma-algebra, using Sion's inner/outer process splitting and closed summation conditions.
result: The regulated domain is identified with the splitting class of Sion's processes; sequential closed summation on a bounded interval is shown equivalent to weak sigma-distributivity of the generated band, and the framework recovers the Volauf and Kusraev–Malyugin extensions plus an exact semivariation-preserving extension.
conclusion: The work provides a unified convergence-theoretic framework for measure extension, generalizing ordered-group and finite-variation measure theories, but it is a pure abstract-measure-theory contribution with no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum platforms.

title: Adaptive Node Distribution Via Probability Density Functions For Birkhoff Pseudospectral Trajectory Optimisation
authors: Xiaofeng Wu Andrian A. Yasintus
abstract: ArXiv:2610.12827v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Pseudospectral methods are a powerful framework for spacecraft trajectory optimisation that rely on fixed, problem-independent collocation nodes such as Legendre-Gauss-Lobatto (LGL) nodes. These nodes are located according to polynomial root distributions, which can result in insufficient resolution in regions of high dynamical activity, such as those encountered during collision avoidance manoeuvres. This paper presents an adaptive node distribution strategy for Birkhoff pseudospectral trajectory optimisation, where the collocation nodes are placed according to a probability density function derived from the thrust magnitude profile of the spacecraft. By concentrating nodes in regions of high dynamical variation, the proposed method simultaneously achieves feasibility preservation and improved convergence with fewer nodes in a collision avoidance case study when compared to the universal Birkhoff method, with Model Predictive Control serving as an independent validation comparator. The case study highlights the practical consequences of inter-node constraint violations and validates the adaptive node scheme as a robust and efficient alternative for fuel-optimal spacecraft manoeuvre design.
tldr: The paper proposes an adaptive node distribution strategy for Birkhoff pseudospectral trajectory optimization, placing collocation nodes according to a probability density function derived from the thrust magnitude profile.
motivation: Fixed collocation nodes in pseudospectral methods can provide insufficient resolution in high-dynamical-activity regions, especially during collision avoidance maneuvers.
method: The authors derive a probability density function from the spacecraft thrust magnitude profile and use it to adaptively distribute Birkhoff pseudospectral collocation nodes.
result: In a collision avoidance case study, the adaptive node scheme achieves feasibility preservation and improved convergence with fewer nodes than the universal Birkhoff method, validated against Model Predictive Control.
conclusion: The adaptive node distribution is a robust and efficient alternative for fuel-optimal spacecraft maneuver design, though it lies outside quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, and hybrid quantum systems.

title: When Solvers Get Moody: Quantifying And Predicting Performance Variability In Mixed Integer Programming
authors: Mourchid Adegbindin, Brenda Dietrich, Jamol Pender, Andrea Lodi
abstract: ArXiv:2610.12876v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Mixed-integer programming (MIP) solvers are widely used, yet their performance can vary substantially even under seemingly neutral perturbations. Such variability complicates benchmarking, and the interpretation of computational studies. We introduce the Weighted Variability Score (WVS), a robust multi-component metric that aggregates dispersion in normalized runtime, final optimality gap, LP iterations, and branch-and-bound nodes across repeated runs. On a large subset of MIPLIB 2017 instances, each solved in 100 randomized runs under a four-hour limit, WVS reveals a right-skewed distribution with a substantial upper tail: many instances are essentially stable, but some exhibit large variability that is not explained by basic properties alone. Notably, this experiment proved optimality for the open instance 'neos-5045105-creuse' in two SCIP runs. Using static descriptors and root-level features, a tree-based predictor with a gated tail uplift achieves a mean absolute error of 0.058 and Spearman rank correlation of 0.65 on a sealed test split. Feature-importance analysis highlights root degeneracy, matrix structure, coefficient ranges, and presolve reductions as the main drivers of high WVS. Because variability is systematic and partially predictable from inexpensive early-run features, our findings offer a practical tool for preemptive tuning and lay a foundation for fairer evaluation of new algorithms.
tldr: The paper introduces a Weighted Variability Score to quantify and predict performance variability of mixed-integer programming solvers across repeated randomized runs.
motivation: MIP solver performance can vary substantially under neutral perturbations, complicating benchmarking and computational studies, so a robust metric and predictor are needed.
method: They run 100 randomized solves per instance on a large MIPLIB 2017 subset with a four-hour limit, define WVS aggregating runtime, gap, LP iterations, and B&B nodes, and train a tree-based predictor with a gated tail uplift using static and root-level features.
result: WVS is right-skewed with a substantial upper tail; the predictor achieves MAE 0.058 and Spearman 0.65 on a sealed test split, with root degeneracy, matrix structure, coefficient ranges, and presolve reductions as key drivers.
conclusion: Solver variability is systematic and partially predictable from inexpensive early-run features, providing a practical tool for preemptive tuning and fairer evaluation of new algorithms.

title: Tight Guarantees For Static Policies In Vehicle Sharing Networks
authors: Jiaqi Shi Adam N. Elmachtoub
abstract: ArXiv:2610.13089v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study pricing in a vehicle sharing network with [MATH] locations and [MATH] vehicles, motivated by on-demand bike, scooter, and car sharing, as well as robotaxi and ride sharing services. Customers request directed trips between locations, with travel times following general distributions, and leave without service if no vehicle is available. Pricing affects both demand for trips and the distribution of vehicles across locations. Computing an optimal dynamic pricing policy is challenging because the system state depends on the number of vehicles available at each location and in transit (including how long they have been traveling), motivating the use of simple static policies that offer a fixed price for each trip. For any number of vehicles and locations, we establish a tight performance guarantee for static pricing relative to optimal dynamic pricing. The guarantee holds for any concave objective functions (including revenue rate) and general travel time distributions. Our tight guarantee is bounded below by [MATH] (over 50%), achieving the first universal, non-asymptotic constant factor guarantee. We also prove that the optimal static policy can be efficiently computed by solving a convex optimization problem. Finally, we extend our performance guarantee to the setting with supply redirection.
tldr: The paper proves tight constant-factor performance guarantees for static pricing policies in vehicle sharing networks relative to optimal dynamic pricing, with an efficiently computable optimal static policy.
motivation: Dynamic pricing in vehicle sharing networks is complex due to high-dimensional system state, so simple static policies are attractive but lacked universal non-asymptotic guarantees.
method: The authors model a vehicle sharing network with general travel time distributions and concave objectives, then derive a tight bound comparing static pricing to optimal dynamic pricing and show the optimal static policy solves a convex optimization problem.
result: They establish a universal constant-factor guarantee bounded below by 1/2 (over 50%) for any number of vehicles and locations, and extend the guarantee to supply redirection settings.
conclusion: Static pricing can provably achieve at least half of the optimal dynamic pricing performance while being computationally tractable, offering a practical alternative for vehicle sharing platforms.

title: Organizational Context For The Enterprise Security Brain
authors: Eden Yavin, Ariel Zadok, Gal Engelberg, Elad Elouz, Leon Goldberg
abstract: ArXiv:2610.12540v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Agents that investigate and decide on enterprise security reason over a machine-readable view of the environment: its assets, identities, configurations, relations, and findings. The correct judgment about an asset also depends on what the organization knows about it: who owns it, what business function it serves, which policy governs it, and which risks were accepted. Part of this knowledge can be inferred from machine state, such as an ownership tag; most of it is recorded by people in policies, audit reports, architecture diagrams, tickets, and conversations, outside machine state. We call this distance the organizational context gap. Closing it poses four challenges: extracting the right claims from heterogeneous organizational data and, at inference time, detecting claims made stale by live state, checking live state against the governing policy, and binding architecture diagrams, which carry the business logic, to live resources. We introduce organizational context as a layer of the enterprise security brain and define it with a taxonomy and six properties its representation must preserve. We then define a context model in which a claim carries one meaning, an attestation records each source that asserts it, strength is derived from live evidence at read time, and claims resolve onto the entities of the asset graph. On a production environment spanning AWS, Okta, Google Workspace, and GitHub, extraction recovers 0.80 of a pooled 1,355-claim ground truth at 0.87 precision, with 0.5% of extracted claims unsupported by their source. An agent reasoning over live state and resolved context raises the conflict in 0.97 of stale-finding tasks, and reaches answer correctness of 0.83 on policy-alignment tasks and 0.86 on architecture tasks.
tldr: The paper introduces an organizational context layer for enterprise security agents, defining a taxonomy and context model to bridge the gap between machine state and human-recorded knowledge.
motivation: Enterprise security agents need rich organizational context—ownership, business function, policies, accepted risks—that is largely absent from machine-readable state, creating an organizational context gap.
method: The authors propose a taxonomy and six properties for organizational context, plus a claim-based context model with attestations, live-evidence strength, and resolution onto an asset graph.
result: In a production environment across AWS, Okta, Google Workspace, and GitHub, extraction recovers 0.80 of a 1,355-claim ground truth at 0.87 precision, and an agent resolves stale findings in 0.97 of tasks with answer correctness of 0.83 on policy tasks and 0.86 on architecture tasks.
conclusion: Organizational context is a necessary layer for enterprise security reasoning, and the proposed representation can improve agent performance on stale-finding, policy-alignment, and architecture tasks.

title: Game Petri Nets: Compositional Modeling And Analysis Of Large-Scale Strategic Systems
authors: Quanyan Zhu
abstract: ArXiv:2610.12779v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large-scale strategic systems, such as maintenance workflows, cyber campaigns, and multi-agent AI pipelines, consist of many interactions whose outcomes determine which later interactions become possible, who takes part, and with what resources. We introduce game Petri nets, formalized as outcome-driven compositional game Petri nets (OCGPNs), to model and analyze such systems. Local games are attached to places of a colored Petri net, and a game-to-token interface converts each resolved game into typed tokens that enable, synchronize, or block subsequent games. For general, concurrent nets, we give an operational semantics and a structural theory based on invariants and Farkas certificates, which shows that guards can certify unreachability whereas incentive instruments can only change values. For sequential nets, the net induces a stochastic game on its game places. We prove that global equilibria are exactly collections of equilibria of local games augmented by continuation values, characterize through successor-level pivotality when downstream games change upstream behavior, and compute values place by place via a decomposition into strongly connected components, at a cost additive in local game sizes. A composition calculus based on place fusion glues certificates across subnets and summarizes downstream subnets by their entry values. Two running examples, a maintenance workflow and an intrusion campaign derived from multi-resolution cyber-defense games, illustrate the theory, including the composition of a newly discovered attack scenario with an existing campaign.
tldr: The paper introduces game Petri nets, formalized as outcome-driven compositional game Petri nets (OCGPNs), for modeling and analyzing large-scale strategic systems via local games attached to colored Petri net places.
motivation: Large-scale strategic systems involve many interdependent interactions whose outcomes determine subsequent possibilities, participants, and resources, requiring a compositional formal framework.
method: The authors attach local games to places of a colored Petri net, define a game-to-token interface, provide operational semantics, structural invariants, Farkas certificates, stochastic game reductions for sequential nets, and a place-fusion composition calculus.
result: They prove global equilibria decompose into local equilibria augmented by continuation values, characterize downstream influence via successor-level pivotality, and compute values via strongly connected component decomposition with additive cost.
conclusion: The framework is illustrated on a maintenance workflow and an intrusion campaign, enabling compositional analysis and certificate gluing across subnets for strategic systems.

title: The False Allure Of "Security By Obscurity": A Game-Theoretic Approach
authors: Sunoo Park In-Uck Park
abstract: ArXiv:2610.12858v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: "Security by obscurity," or the idea that hiding how a system works helps protect it from adversaries, has long been poorly regarded in the security community. Yet its intuitive appeal persists, and it has resurfaced repeatedly in industry practices and public debates over the years. The logic, on the one hand, is that open scrutiny of systems is the best way to find and respond to problems; and on the other hand, that too much openness can increase risk by giving adversaries a roadmap for attack. This isn't purely a technical question, but a human one: it's about how attackers and good-faith security researchers respond to openness in the real world. As such, security experts base their stance on decades of community experience; however, the field lacks empirical or theoretical foundations to back up these long-standing beliefs. We provide the first rigorous modeling of "security by obscurity," aiming to capture how rational actors will respond to openness or obscurity in fallible systems. We prove that in equilibrium under realistic model conditions, "obscured" systems are more likely to suffer successful attacks than "open" systems --- establishing theoretical support for the longstanding received wisdom.
tldr: This paper provides a game-theoretic model showing that, under realistic conditions, obscured systems are more likely to suffer successful attacks than open systems, offering theoretical support for the security community's preference for openness.
motivation: The long-standing belief that 'security by obscurity' is harmful lacks rigorous theoretical or empirical foundations, despite its persistence in industry and public debate.
method: The authors construct a game-theoretic model of rational attackers and good-faith security researchers responding to openness or obscurity in fallible systems, and analyze equilibrium outcomes.
result: They prove that under realistic model conditions, obscured systems are more likely to be successfully attacked than open systems, establishing a theoretical basis for the received wisdom.
conclusion: The work formalizes the debate over security by obscurity and supports the view that openness improves security in equilibrium.

title: Toward Maximizing Algebraic Connectivity Via Density-Dependent Backbone Construction And Reinforcement Learning Completion
authors: Zeru Zhu, Marco Gamarra, Ji Liu
abstract: ArXiv:2610.12697v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper studies an open network design problem of constructing graph topologies with maximum algebraic connectivity under fixed numbers of vertices and edges. A density-dependent approach is proposed that decomposes the design task into two stages: a high-quality, low-cost structural backbone construction and a reinforcement learning completion stage. The method selects the backbone based on density, using complete multipartite graphs in dense regimes and Cayley graphs in low-to-intermediate regimes, and then refines the remaining edges through a learning-based procedure. Numerical results show that the proposed method achieves high algebraic connectivity with favorable runtime scalability, outperforming existing methods. These results support a structural-family-first strategy for scalable network design.
tldr: This paper proposes a density-dependent two-stage method combining structural backbone construction with reinforcement learning to maximize the algebraic connectivity of graphs under fixed vertex and edge counts.
motivation: The authors aim to solve the open network design problem of constructing graph topologies with maximum algebraic connectivity, which is relevant for network robustness and synchronization.
method: The approach selects either complete multipartite graphs or Cayley graphs as a backbone depending on graph density, then refines the remaining edges via a reinforcement learning completion procedure.
result: Numerical experiments show the method achieves high algebraic connectivity with favorable runtime scalability, outperforming existing baseline methods.
conclusion: A structural-family-first strategy with learning-based refinement is effective for scalable network design, though the work is purely classical graph optimization.

title: A Palais-Smale Type Condition For Optimal Control Problems
authors: Jean-Michel Coron, Li Deng, Xu Zhang
abstract: ArXiv:2610.13070v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider an optimal control problem with a general control constraint and a fixed initial state, for which convexity assumptions are absent. To establish the existence of optimal pairs, we introduce a control version of the Palais-Smale type condition adapted from critical point theory and prove that optimal pairs exist under this condition (see Theorem 2.1). Subsequently, we verify that a specific class of optimal control problems satisfies our Palais-Smale type condition (see Proposition 2.1). Furthermore, as an application, we present an example (Example 3.1) and show that, to the best of our knowledge, no existing result can be applied to establish the existence of an optimal pair in this case (see Section 3.1.1). Example 3.2 shows that finitely many Pontryagin maximum principle candidates do not guarantee the existence of an optimal control. Finally, Example 3.3 demonstrates that the proposed Palais-Smale type condition is sufficient, but not necessary, for the existence of optimal controls.
tldr: The paper introduces a control-theoretic Palais-Smale condition to prove existence of optimal pairs in nonconvex optimal control problems where standard convexity assumptions fail.
motivation: Existence of optimal controls is difficult without convexity assumptions, and classical results such as the Pontryagin maximum principle may not guarantee an optimal pair.
method: The authors adapt the Palais-Smale condition from critical point theory to optimal control settings, prove an existence theorem under this condition, and verify it for a specific problem class.
result: They establish existence of optimal pairs via the new condition, provide examples where existing results do not apply, and show that finitely many Pontryagin maximum principle candidates do not ensure an optimal control.
conclusion: The proposed Palais-Smale type condition is sufficient but not necessary for existence of optimal controls, offering a new tool for nonconvex optimal control problems.

title: A Ray-Traced Digital Twin For 5g Nr Positioning With OpenAirInterface
authors: Nima Chaharbaghi, Florian Kaltenberger, Bartosz Podrygajlo, Rakesh Mundlamuri, Roberto Verdone
abstract: ArXiv:2610.13138v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Evaluating 5G positioning on a physical testbed ties every measurement to one propagation environment and one antenna layout, so any question about an alternative deployment requires a new field campaign. We present a ray-traced digital twin of the GEO-5G testbed at EURECOM that drives an unmodified OpenAirInterface (OAI) 5G stack with per-antenna channels computed by Sionna-RT over a 3D model of the site. The distributed gNB antennas are modelled as independent radio devices rather than as elements of a compact array, which preserves the per-antenna absolute delays on which time-difference-of-arrival (TDoA) positioning depends. With them preserved, the twin drives OAI's SRS-based UL-TDoA pipeline to metre-level accuracy consistent with that reported for the physical deployment. We then use the twin to answer a question the physical testbed cannot. Widening the carrier truncates the tail of the horizontal error distribution without improving a typical position, and leaves the vertical error untouched, because the latter is limited by the array geometry rather than by the measurement. That limit is predictable from the antenna coordinates alone, and a height-diverse layout reduces the RMS height error by a factor of four.
tldr: A ray-traced digital twin of the EURECOM GEO-5G testbed drives an unmodified OpenAirInterface 5G stack to evaluate uplink TDoA positioning and explore deployment alternatives.
motivation: Physical 5G positioning testbeds bind every measurement to a single propagation environment and antenna layout, so evaluating alternative deployments requires costly new field campaigns.
method: Per-antenna channels are computed with Sionna-RT ray tracing over a 3D site model and fed into an unmodified OAI 5G stack; distributed gNB antennas are treated as independent radios to preserve the absolute per-antenna delays needed for UL-TDoA, and the twin is then used to test carrier bandwidth and antenna-layout variations.
result: The twin reproduces metre-level UL-TDoA accuracy consistent with the physical deployment; widening the carrier truncates the tail of the horizontal error distribution without improving typical accuracy or vertical error, while a height-diverse antenna layout reduces RMS height error by a factor of four.
conclusion: Ray-traced digital twins can faithfully emulate 5G positioning testbeds and answer deployment questions impractical to address experimentally, with vertical accuracy fundamentally limited by array geometry.

title: Homard: Hammering Off-chip Memory Via Aggregate Power Rail Disclosure
authors: Eliott Qu\'er\'e, Li-Chung Chiang, Carina Fiedler, Thomas Rokicki, Maria M\'endez Real, Alessandro Palumbo, Lilian Bossuet, Rub\'en Salvador, Daniel Gruss
abstract: ArXiv:2610.12621v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Software-based microarchitectural attacks have mainly exploited timing differences to infer information from DRAM. However, defenses and optimizations can prevent timing-based approaches from resolving precise microarchitectural behaviors. We show that unprivileged millisecond- and milliampere-resolution power sensors on modern Arm SoCs can recover DRAM mapping functions and reveal the data dependence of memory accesses without timers. We present HOMARD, a methodology that reads DRAM activity from this telemetry, and two attack primitives. HOMARD-RE is a hierarchy-aware linear-algebraic method that reverse-engineers DRAM addressing functions from power alone. HOMARD-DATA recovers the Hamming weight of a fetched cache line through joint-power rail templating and secret byte values through correlation power analysis on the same rails. Across an AMD ZCU102, a Raspberry Pi 5, and a multi-chip-based LPDDR4 NVIDIA Jetson TX2, HOMARD-RE succeeds where row-buffer timing methods fail. On the Pi 5, HOMARD-DATA classifies 9 Hamming-weight levels at 81.5% accuracy and recovers secret bytes in minutes by correlating rail current with data-dependent bit toggling between neighbors in a row. Both primitives work with an architectural load or a mispredicted Spectre-RSB path on which no value is architecturally read. These results establish unprivileged power telemetry as an independent side channel for profiled microarchitectural attacks, particularly when timing falls silent.
tldr: HOMARD exploits unprivileged power telemetry on Arm SoCs to reverse-engineer DRAM addressing and recover memory data, providing a side channel when timing attacks fail.
motivation: Timing-based microarchitectural attacks on DRAM are increasingly thwarted by defenses and optimizations, motivating alternative side channels that do not rely on timers.
method: The authors use millisecond- and milliampere-resolution power sensors on Arm SoCs, developing hierarchy-aware linear-algebraic reverse-engineering of DRAM addressing (HOMARD-RE) and joint power-rail templating plus correlation power analysis to recover Hamming weights and secret bytes (HOMARD-DATA).
result: Across AMD ZCU102, Raspberry Pi 5, and NVIDIA Jetson TX2, HOMARD-RE succeeds where row-buffer timing fails; on Raspberry Pi 5, HOMARD-DATA classifies 9 Hamming-weight levels at 81.5% accuracy and recovers secret bytes in minutes, even via mispredicted Spectre-RSB paths.
conclusion: Unprivileged power telemetry is established as an independent side channel for profiled microarchitectural attacks, particularly when timing channels are silent.

title: Pvbrf-id: Private, Verifiable And Byzantine-Robust Federated Intrusion Detection For Oilfield Enterprise Networks
authors: Mustafa S. Aljumaily, Ali Ataeemh Allami, Mustafa N. Mnati, Nawar S. Alseelawi, Shahab Abdulla
abstract: ArXiv:2610.12704v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Federated learning allows dispersed oilfield sites to train a shared intrusion detector without pooling network traffic, yet its aggregation step forces a choice between privacy and robustness. Byzantine-robust rules must read each update in the clear, whereas secure aggregation hides updates from the checks that detect poisoning. We present PVBRF-ID, a two-server protocol in which sites secret-share their updates and the servers jointly test each update's norm and its cosine similarity to a reference computed on a small clean root set, revealing one accept bit per site. Commitments, Merkle roots and a homomorphic audit make the inclusion of accepted updates publicly verifiable. On a 15-class Edge-IIoTset task with ten sites holding differently distributed data and ten random seeds, PVBRF-ID matched FedAvg on clean data (macro-F1 0.708 vs. 0.706) and withstood sign-flip attacks (0.696 vs. 0.091). Against an adaptive attacker controlling 30% of sites, PVBRF-ID with secure clipping reached 0.641, whereas FedAvg fell to 0.046; plaintext multi-Krum remained higher by 0.052. An update-inference attacker recovered each site's class mix from plaintext updates (Spearman correlation 0.81) but not from one server's view. Backdoors passed the filter, and noise-based mitigation gave only heuristic protection. The implementation uses Python 3.13, NumPy 2.3, 30 rounds and 10 seeds.
tldr: PVBRF-ID is a two-server federated learning protocol for privacy-preserving, verifiable, and Byzantine-robust intrusion detection in oilfield enterprise networks.
motivation: Federated intrusion detection must balance privacy via secure aggregation against robustness to poisoning attacks, which existing methods trade off.
method: Sites secret-share model updates; two servers jointly test each update's norm and cosine similarity to a reference from a clean root set, producing one accept bit per site, with commitments, Merkle roots, and a homomorphic audit for public verifiability.
result: On a 15-class Edge-IIoTset task with ten sites, PVBRF-ID matched FedAvg on clean data, withstood sign-flip and adaptive attackers better than FedAvg, but backdoors passed the filter and noise-based mitigation was only heuristic.
conclusion: The protocol provides private, verifiable, and Byzantine-robust aggregation for federated intrusion detection but does not solve backdoor filtering and is unrelated to quantum information research.

title: Power, Performance, And Area Of HPC-Based Malware Detectors: An Fpga And Open-PDK Asic Study
authors: Alireza Abolhasani Zeraatkar, Parnian Shabani Kamran, Parsa Mirfasihi, Saleh Khalaj Monfared, Hussain Al-Asaad
abstract: ArXiv:2610.12795v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Hardware malware detectors (HMDs) classify programs as benign or malicious based on hardware performance counter (HPC) data. Previous studies have shown that ensemble classifiers outperform other classifiers on detection metrics. However, the area, power, and timing costs of HMDs remain open questions. We address these questions across a comprehensive design space comprising multiple classifier families, variable HPC sets, and ensemble learning methods. We designed a pipeline to reconstruct selected trained models, generate synthesizable register-transfer-level (RTL) implementations, validate each design against a bit-accurate golden model, and evaluate the implementations. The results show that tree- and rule-based detectors achieve the highest detection performance with nearly an order of magnitude less area and several times lower energy than function-based classifiers. Reducing the number of HPC inputs to fit a processor's concurrent-counter limit preserves detection performance while substantially reducing area, power, and delay.
tldr: This paper evaluates the power, performance, and area costs of hardware malware detectors (HMDs) implemented on FPGAs and open-PDK ASICs using hardware performance counter (HPC) data.
motivation: While prior work showed ensemble classifiers outperform other classifiers for HMD detection metrics, the area, power, and timing costs of such detectors remained open questions worth addressing across a broad design space.
method: The authors built a pipeline that reconstructs trained models, generates synthesizable RTL implementations, validates each design against a bit-accurate golden model, and evaluates them across classifier families, HPC sets, and ensemble methods.
result: Tree- and rule-based detectors achieve the best detection performance with nearly an order of magnitude less area and several times lower energy than function-based classifiers, and reducing HPC inputs preserves performance while cutting area, power, and delay.
conclusion: The study provides a comprehensive cost characterization of HMD designs, showing that ensemble/tree-based classifiers offer favorable area-power-performance trade-offs for hardware malware detection.

title: APEX-Harm: Evaluating Agent Safety In Shared Professional Workspaces
authors: Ziyi Yang, Adel Bibi, Guohao Li, Bernard Ghanem, Carlos Hinojosa
abstract: ArXiv:2610.13623v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Professional agents increasingly work through command-line interfaces and multiple tools over shared workspaces containing files, messages, and business applications. These environments create safety risks that are difficult to capture with attacks placed at a single, known read location. We introduce APEX-Harm, a benchmark for evaluating prompt and script injection against long-horizon agents performing finance, consulting, and legal tasks in large workspaces. Each task contains 115 to 328 files, together with email, calendar, chat, document, spreadsheet, PDF, and code-execution tools exposed through MCP servers. The benchmark includes six attack categories covering static and dynamic injections, task-specific script replacement, and attacker-provided generic scripts, and evaluates attack success, exposure, and task performance. We evaluate 12 frontier models on 180 task instances per model. Opus 5 and Sonnet 5 have the lowest overall attack success rates (8% and 20%), while task-specific script replacement and attacker-provided generic script attacks remain substantially more effective, averaging 81-84% and 73% attack success, respectively. Gemini 3.8 Flash achieves the highest mean task score (0.877) while still exhibiting a 33% attack success rate. These results show that completing the requested task is not sufficient evidence of safe behavior: an agent can produce a correct deliverable while also performing an unauthorized action in the workspace.
tldr: APEX-Harm is a benchmark for evaluating prompt- and script-injection attacks against long-horizon LLM agents operating in shared professional workspaces with many files and MCP-exposed tools.
motivation: Agents increasingly act over shared workspaces containing files, messages, and business applications, creating security risks that single-location, known-read attacks fail to capture.
method: The benchmark constructs finance, consulting, and legal tasks each with 115-328 files plus email, calendar, chat, document, spreadsheet, PDF, and code-execution tools via MCP servers, and defines six attack categories covering static/dynamic injection and script replacement, measuring attack success, exposure, and task performance across 12 frontier models.
result: Opus 5 and Sonnet 5 show the lowest overall attack success (8% and 20%), while task-specific script replacement and attacker-provided generic scripts remain far more effective (81-84% and 73%); Gemini 3.8 Flash attains the highest mean task score (0.877) while still suffering 33% attack success.
conclusion: Correct task completion is not sufficient evidence of safe behavior, since agents can deliver valid outputs while simultaneously performing unauthorized workspace actions.

title: Minimax Rates For Estimating Powered Sliced Wasserstein Functionals
authors: Binh Thuan Tran
abstract: ArXiv:2610.12740v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the two-sample estimation of the powered Sliced Wasserstein functional under projected [MATH]-th moment assumptions. Let [MATH], where [MATH] and [MATH] are two sample sizes. We establish the minimax rates in the noncritical regimes. When [MATH], the minimax risk is of order [MATH], while for [MATH] it is of order [MATH]. In both cases, the natural plug-in estimator is minimax rate-optimal. At the endpoint [MATH], the minimax risk is bounded away from zero, so uniformly consistent estimation is impossible. At the critical order [MATH], we obtain the exact worst-case rate of the plug-in estimator and a lower bound for the minimax risk, leaving a logarithmic gap between the lower and upper bounds. The exact minimax rate in this critical case remains open.
tldr: The paper establishes minimax rates for estimating the powered Sliced Wasserstein functional in a two-sample setting under projected moment assumptions.
motivation: Sliced Wasserstein distances are widely used in statistics and machine learning as computationally tractable alternatives to the Wasserstein distance, but the optimal estimation rates for their powered functionals were not fully characterized.
method: The authors analyze the plug-in estimator for the powered Sliced Wasserstein functional, deriving minimax upper and lower bounds across noncritical, endpoint, and critical regimes defined by the relationship between the power parameter and the sample sizes.
result: Minimax risk scales as one rate when the power exceeds half the total sample size and another rate otherwise, with the plug-in estimator being rate-optimal; at the endpoint uniform consistency is impossible, and at the critical order a logarithmic gap remains between lower and upper bounds.
conclusion: The plug-in estimator is minimax rate-optimal in all noncritical regimes, while the exact minimax rate at the critical order remains an open problem.

title: Reflexivity Of Grothendieck Spaces And Strongly Normal Sequences
authors: Wies{\l}aw \'sliwa
abstract: ArXiv:2610.12787v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A normalized sequence [MATH] in the dual [MATH] of a Banach space [MATH] is called normal if it is weak-star null, and strongly normal if [ G(y_n)=^{\infty}|y_n(x)|<\infty\right} ] is dense in [MATH]. We prove that, within the class of Grothendieck Banach spaces, reflexivity is characterized by the subsequence behavior of normal sequences: a Grothendieck space [MATH] is reflexive if and only if every normal sequence in [MATH] contains a strongly normal subsequence. If [MATH] is nonreflexive and Grothendieck, then [MATH] contains a normalized weakly null sequence none of whose subsequences is strongly normal; more strongly, it contains a closed hereditarily [MATH] subspace [MATH] with a normalized weakly null Schauder basis such that no sequence in [MATH] is strongly normal. We also obtain an exact quotient criterion valid for arbitrary Banach spaces: a normal sequence has a strongly normal subsequence precisely when, for some subsequence [MATH], the quotient [MATH] is separable. The proofs combine a weak-star basic-sequence argument with results of Haydon, Johnson--Maurey--Schechtman and Popov. Concrete realizations are given in [MATH] for nonatomic probability spaces (and, more generally, for [MATH]-finite spaces with a nonatomic part) and in [MATH].
tldr: The paper characterizes reflexivity of Grothendieck Banach spaces via the existence of strongly normal subsequences in normal (weak-star null, normalized) sequences in the dual space.
motivation: The authors aim to connect Banach space geometry (reflexivity, Grothendieck property) with the sequential structure of weak-star null normalized sequences, providing a functional-analytic characterization of reflexivity.
method: The proofs combine a weak-star basic-sequence argument with results of Haydon, Johnson–Maurey–Schechtman, and Popov, and an exact quotient criterion for arbitrary Banach spaces involving separability of quotients.
result: A Grothendieck space is reflexive iff every normal sequence in its dual contains a strongly normal subsequence; for nonreflexive Grothendieck spaces one can build a hereditarily c0 subspace with a normalized weakly null Schauder basis whose sequences are never strongly normal.
conclusion: The work yields a purely sequence-based characterization of reflexivity among Grothendieck spaces and concrete realizations in L1 of nonatomic probability spaces and in C(K).

title: Safety Graph: When Safety Responses Become Attack Surfaces In Cyber-Physical Systems
authors: Rakesh Podder, Philip D. Hopkins, Sarath Sreedharan, Indrakshi Ray, Indrajit Ray
abstract: ArXiv:2610.13086v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Modern industrial control systems (ICS) are susceptible to cyber attacks triggering safety failures in the operational technology (OT) layer. The traditional way to mitigate any failure in OT is to implement safety responses. However, we show in this work that these responses can open up new attack surfaces, thereby vastly expanding the scope of lateral movement. Existing frameworks model cyber-to-physical escalation but provide no mechanism to reason about how these safety responses to OT-failures can trigger new cascading cyber attacks in the Information Technology (IT) layer. To enable such reasoning, we introduce Safety Graph (SG), a formal framework unifying three paradigms - Attack Graphs (AG), Fault Trees (FT), and Event Trees (ET) - over a shared propositional state space, capturing the full bidirectional IT-OT cascade. We provide a sound and complete compilation of SG to a classical AI planning problem, performing plan search using A* to find cross-layer cascade paths. Through a Web3D modeling and simulation of the Tennessee Eastman chemical process plant, which is a widely used chemical engineering benchmark serving as a standard for testing control, monitoring and fault propagation, we demonstrate that the planning compilation of SG automatically discovers safety-response-induced lateral movements, and identifies the responsible barriers that are unidentifiable under existing models. A complexity and scalability analysis characterizes how the planning compilation of SG scales with model size and cascade depth. To the best of our knowledge, SG is the first framework to formally model IT-OT attacks and enable operators to explore the problem of cyber attacks triggering cascading failures in ICS.
tldr: The paper introduces Safety Graph (SG), a formal framework that unifies attack graphs, fault trees, and event trees to model how safety responses in industrial control systems can create new cyber attack surfaces and cascading IT-OT failures.
motivation: Safety responses deployed to mitigate operational technology failures in industrial control systems can themselves become attack surfaces, but existing cyber-physical security frameworks cannot reason about how such responses trigger new cascading attacks in the IT layer.
