conclusion: For platforms, disclosure can alter borrower fees without changing lending volume, and wider information access need not lower fees; effects depend on recipient and demand-supply balance.

title: Decision-Focused Learning For Cyber-Physical Risk-Aware Power Grid Operations
authors: Ayesha Siddiqua Dina, Ebisa D. Wollega, Afzal Hossain Sohag
abstract: ArXiv:2610.13853v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Power grid cyber-physical security requires intrusion detection methods that account for the operational consequences of detection errors. However, the existing intrusion detection approaches primarily focus on the predictive performance of learning algorithms, while downstream operational costs are often optimized independently, which can lead to inferior operational performance. To help alleviate this problem, we propose a novel optimization-learning cyber-physical-risk-informed framework that communicates iteratively to minimize power grid operational costs. This framework translates machine learning prediction errors into power grid operational cyber-physical-risk costs. Experimental results on two power grid operation datasets, Industrial Control System (ICS) Cyber Attack and Sherlock, show that the proposed approach improves power grid operation costs compared with the traditional approach.
tldr: The paper proposes a decision-focused learning framework that integrates machine learning prediction errors into cyber-physical risk costs to improve power grid operational decisions.
motivation: Existing intrusion detection methods for power grids optimize predictive accuracy separately from downstream operational costs, potentially leading to suboptimal operational performance.
method: The authors develop an optimization-learning framework that iteratively communicates between a learner and a power grid operational model, translating prediction errors into operational risk costs.
result: Experiments on the ICS Cyber Attack and Sherlock datasets show that the proposed approach reduces power grid operation costs compared to traditional methods.
conclusion: Decision-focused learning can improve cyber-physical security operations by directly accounting for operational consequences rather than only predictive performance.

title: Median Randomized quasi-Monte Carlo For Nested Integration
authors: Arved Bartuska, Yang Liu, Ra\'{u}l Tempone
abstract: ArXiv:2610.12643v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Nested integrals [MATH] where [MATH] and [MATH] frequently arise in Bayesian experimental design, medical decision making, and computational finance. Statistical estimators for nested integrals are more computationally demanding than for standard integrals. Recent studies demonstrate that the median randomized quasi-Monte Carlo (mRQMC) method achieves super-polynomial convergence rates for analytic integrands. We extend mRQMC methods to nested integrations and propose a novel double-loop mRQMC estimator with super-polynomial convergence rate if both the inner and outer integrands are analytic. Established estimators for nested integrals, such as double-loop or multilevel Monte Carlo, are by contrast limited to algebraic convergence rates. However, expected information gain (EIG) applications from experimental design typically do not fulfill this condition due to a lack of regularity in the outer integrand. We address this through a theoretically-grounded importance sampling regularization scheme. Although super-polynomial convergence rates remain achievable for the inner integral, only the algebraic rate [MATH] for any [MATH] can be theoretically guaranteed for the outer integral in the EIG, where [MATH] denotes the order of the mixed derivatives of the regularized outer integrand. Our approach shows substantial improvements over double-loop randomized quasi-Monte Carlo methods based on the sample mean in moderately high-dimensional settings for a simple polynomial example. Moreover, we demonstrate improved convergence behavior of the median-based estimator for the more challenging setting of EIG estimation.
tldr: The paper develops a double-loop median randomized quasi-Monte Carlo estimator for nested integrals and applies it to expected information gain estimation.
motivation: Nested integrals are computationally demanding in Bayesian experimental design, medical decision making, and computational finance, where existing Monte Carlo estimators achieve only algebraic convergence rates.
method: The authors extend median randomized quasi-Monte Carlo to nested integration, propose a double-loop mRQMC estimator with super-polynomial convergence for analytic integrands, and introduce an importance sampling regularization scheme for expected information gain.
result: The proposed estimator achieves super-polynomial convergence when both inner and outer integrands are analytic, while for EIG applications only an algebraic rate can be guaranteed for the outer integral, with empirical improvements over double-loop randomized quasi-Monte Carlo.
conclusion: The work advances numerical methods for nested integration and EIG estimation, showing improved convergence behavior, but it lies outside quantum information, information thermodynamics, quantum networks, and hybrid quantum systems.

title: Complexity Of Multiblock Convex-Concave Saddle-Point Problems With General Smooth Coupling
authors: Nhat Trung Nguyen, Ivan Dorofeev, Irina Podlipnova, Yuriy Dorn, Alexander Gasnikov
abstract: ArXiv:2610.12656v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study multiblock convex--concave saddle-point problems of the form [MATH], with separately charged partial-gradient oracles for all three objective components. We impose joint smoothness and strong convexity bounds on the functions [MATH] and [MATH], together with blockwise Lipschitz conditions on the partial gradients of [MATH], so that the resulting oracle complexities reflect the smoothness and dependency parameters specific to each oracle. Under strong convexity, we develop a randomized lifted extragradient method that achieves linear convergence while providing simultaneous complexity guarantees for all oracles. The partial-gradient complexities for [MATH] and [MATH] exhibit the expected square-root dependence on the corresponding block condition numbers, whereas the coupling-gradient complexities depend on the associated curvature-normalized smoothness parameters. Finite-dimensional bilinear subclasses provide lower-complexity benchmarks within a randomized blockwise linear-span model. When strong convexity of [MATH] and [MATH] is not assumed, a regularization argument yields expected restricted-gap guarantees with accuracy dependence [MATH] for the objective-gradient oracles and [MATH] for the coupling-gradient oracles, up to logarithmic factors. Experiments show observed oracle savings and runtime improvements in regimes of poor objective conditioning.
tldr: The paper analyzes oracle complexity of multiblock convex-concave saddle-point problems with general smooth coupling, developing randomized lifted extragradient methods with linear convergence and matching lower bounds.
motivation: Multiblock saddle-point problems with separately charged partial-gradient oracles arise in structured large-scale optimization, but their complexity under general smooth coupling had not been fully characterized.
method: The authors develop a randomized lifted extragradient method exploiting joint smoothness and strong convexity, with separate oracle accounting for the three objective components, plus a regularization argument for the non-strongly-convex case and bilinear lower-bound benchmarks.
result: They obtain linear convergence with square-root dependence on block condition numbers for the objective oracles, curvature-normalized smoothness dependence for the coupling oracle, and expected restricted-gap guarantees of appropriate accuracy dependence when strong convexity is dropped.
conclusion: The work gives a refined, oracle-specific complexity theory for multiblock convex-concave saddle-point problems, with experiments confirming oracle savings in poorly conditioned regimes.

title: When Is Hotelling's $t^2$ Asymptotically $F$-distributed?
authors: Yanpeng Li, Guangming Pan, Wang Zhou
abstract: ArXiv:2610.12903v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For Gaussian observations, a deterministic multiple of Hotelling's [MATH] statistic has an exact [MATH] distribution. This paper investigates when this approximation remains valid for an independent and identically distributed (i.i.d.) data matrix [MATH] with a fixed, possibly heavy-tailed entry law [MATH]. Under symmetry and [MATH], we prove that approximation by the [MATH] distribution in Kolmogorov distance is equivalent to belonging to the domain of attraction of the normal law. Both conditions are equivalent to relative concentration of the diagonal entries of the null-space projection [MATH]. The central quantity [MATH] measures the geometric alignment between the averaging direction and the random row space of [MATH]. For symmetric finite-variance entries, the sufficient approximation extends to every sequence [MATH] when [MATH], and obtain the [MATH] approximation as a consequence. Centered standardized Pareto laws show that the exponent [MATH] is sharp for this universal absolute-tail sufficient condition, although balanced-tail nonsymmetric laws can retain the approximation at the boundary, which reveals that the asymmetry of the tails matters for the [MATH] approximation.
tags: domain of attraction of the normal law
tldr: The paper characterizes when Hotelling's T² statistic, computed on i.i.d. data with possibly heavy-tailed entries, is asymptotically F-distributed in Kolmogorov distance.
motivation: For Gaussian observations a scaled Hotelling T² follows an exact F distribution, but it is unclear when this classical approximation survives for non-Gaussian, heavy-tailed i.i.d. data.
method: The authors analyze the geometric quantity measuring alignment between the averaging direction and the random row space of the data matrix, using Kolmogorov-distance bounds, symmetry and finite-variance assumptions, and Pareto-law counterexamples.
result: F-approximation holds iff the entry law lies in the domain of attraction of the normal law, equivalently iff the null-space projection diagonal entries relatively concentrate; a universal sufficient condition holds for every sequence when d/n → 0, and the exponent is shown sharp via centered standardized Pareto laws.
conclusion: Asymptotic F-approximation of Hotelling's T² is governed by normal-domain attraction and tail symmetry of the underlying distribution, extending classical Gaussian results to heavy-tailed settings.
keywords: domain of attraction of the normal law

title: Robust Halo Orbit Stationkeeping Under Missed Thrust Events And Maneuver Execution Errors
authors: Kenshiro Oguri Shaurya Shrivastava
abstract: ArXiv:2610.12906v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Spacecraft stationkeeping is subject to various operational uncertainties such as missed thrust events, maneuver execution errors, and dynamics modeling errors. Missed thrust events are the most disruptive of these, and current practices mitigate that risk through Monte Carlo-driven heuristics and conservative margins that offer no formal safety guarantees and do not scale to multiple missed thrust events. This paper models these unplanned thruster outages through the Markov Jump System framework, and represents maneuver execution errors and dynamics linearization errors as bounded multiplicative noise. The resulting closed-loop system is a linear time-varying periodic Markov jump system with multiplicative noise, for which Lyapunov-like mean square stability and periodic set invariance conditions are derived. A linear matrix inequality-based optimal controller synthesis framework then designs a periodic, mode-dependent mean-square stable feedback policy that respects path constraints with probability one. The framework is demonstrated on the Earth-Moon 9:2 near-rectilinear halo orbit (NRHO), under both impulsive and low-thrust propulsion, and on a Saturn-Enceladus [MATH] NRHO using impulsive propulsion. Nonlinear Monte Carlo simulations show that the spacecraft recovers from an arbitrary number of missed thrust events while respecting path constraints, and that the multiplicative noise model introduces additional robustness to maneuver execution error and linearization error.
tldr: This paper develops a Markov Jump System framework with multiplicative noise and LMI-based controller synthesis for robust spacecraft halo orbit stationkeeping under missed thrust events and maneuver execution errors.
motivation: Missed thrust events and maneuver execution errors threaten spacecraft stationkeeping, but current practice relies on Monte Carlo heuristics and conservative margins lacking formal safety guarantees or scalability to multiple outages.
method: Unplanned thruster outages are modeled as a Markov Jump System, and maneuver execution and linearization errors as bounded multiplicative noise, yielding a linear time-varying periodic Markov jump system for which Lyapunov-like mean-square stability and periodic set invariance conditions are derived, enabling an LMI-based mode-dependent periodic feedback controller respecting path constraints with probability one.
result: The framework is demonstrated on the Earth-Moon 9:2 NRHO (impulsive and low-thrust) and a Saturn-Enceladus NRHO, with nonlinear Monte Carlo simulations showing recovery from an arbitrary number of missed thrust events while respecting path constraints.
conclusion: The proposed LMI-based mean-square stabilizing control framework provides formal robustness guarantees for stationkeeping under thruster outages and execution errors, improving on heuristic margins and scaling to multiple missed thrust events.

title: Ader-zist - A Mixed Explicit Ader-dg And Zonally Implicit Space-time Dg Approach For Cartesian Cut Cell Meshes
authors: Michael Dumbser, Christian Engwer, Sandra May, Peter Munch
abstract: ArXiv:2610.13245v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present high order accurate mixed explicit-implicit discontinuous Galerkin (DG) schemes for the solution of hyperbolic systems of conservation laws on Cartesian cut cell meshes. Such meshes may contain arbitrarily small cut cells, which leads to the well-known small cell problem: the CFL condition of explicit schemes would severely restrict the admissible time step. To overcome this difficulty, we use high order explicit fully-discrete one-step ADER-DG schemes only on Cartesian cells away from the embedded boundaries. The zone close to the embedded boundary, which consists of cut cells and their direct face neighbors, is discretized with an implicit space-time DG scheme that is coupled to the explicit scheme directly via the numerical flux. The resulting scheme, called ADER-ZIST (ADER-DG with Zonally Implicit Space-Time DG), is conservative by construction, and its time step is determined only by the size of the Cartesian background cells. Curved embedded boundaries are represented by high order isoparametric sub-triangles inside the cut cells, and the nonlinear system of the implicit cells is solved via an inexact matrix-free Newton-Krylov method. For problems with shock waves, we add an artificial viscosity term whose strength is controlled by an oscillation-eliminating smoothness sensor. ADER-ZIST is assessed on a comprehensive set of test problems for the compressible Euler equations, ranging from smooth flows around straight and curved embedded boundaries to acoustic scattering and shock-dominated flows. The scheme essentially reaches its nominal order of accuracy N+1 for smooth solutions and for polynomial degrees up to N=5, on meshes with minimal volume fractions of the small cut cells down to the order of 10^-7.
tldr: The paper introduces ADER-ZIST, a hybrid explicit-implicit discontinuous Galerkin scheme for solving hyperbolic conservation laws on Cartesian cut cell meshes, addressing the small cell problem near embedded boundaries.
motivation: Explicit DG schemes on cut cell meshes suffer from a severe CFL restriction due to arbitrarily small cut cells near embedded boundaries, making standard time-stepping impractical.
method: The scheme applies high order explicit one-step ADER-DG only on regular Cartesian cells, while cut cells and their face neighbors are treated with an implicit space-time DG method coupled through the numerical flux, with curved boundaries represented via isoparametric sub-triangles and implicit systems solved by a matrix-free Newton-Krylov method.
result: ADER-ZIST is conservative by construction, with time step limited only by the background Cartesian cell size, and achieves nominal order N+1 for polynomial degrees up to N=5 even on meshes with cut cell volume fractions as small as 10^-7, validated on compressible Euler test problems including shocks and acoustic scattering.
conclusion: The mixed explicit-implicit scheme successfully overcomes the small cell problem for cut cell meshes while maintaining high order accuracy and conservation.

title: Optimal Control Of Prox-Regular Sweeping Processes With Variable Time
authors: Tan H. Cao, Boris S. Mordukhovich, Trang Nguyen, Thi Phung
abstract: ArXiv:2610.13327v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The paper is devoted to a broad class of optimal control problems governed by constrained sweeping processes with controlled dynamics, controlled prox-regular moving sets, and variable time included in the optimization process. Employing an advanced version of the method of discrete approximations, we verify its well-posedness with appropriate strong convergence of feasible and optimal solutions. This approach leads us to considering a parametric family of discrete-time controlled sweeping processes, which are reduced in turn to nondynamic mathematical programs with special types of geometric and functional constraints. Invoking powerful tools of first-order and second-order variational analysis and generalized differentiation, we derive necessary optimality conditions for discrete-time and then---by passing to the limit over the diminishing step of discretization---continuous-time controlled sweeping processes. A crucial role in our device is played by explicit coderivative evaluations of set-valued mapping associated with the sweeping dynamics. In this way, we establish novel necessary optimality conditions for local minimizers of continuous-time controlled sweeping processes that contain absolutely continuous and BV adjoint arcs, local and global maximization conditions, [MATH] active set multipliers, vector measures generated by sweeping and control constraints, and free-time transversality condition expressed through the averaged Hamiltonian. For suitably selected multipliers, we also obtain nondegenerate forms of these conditions when the optimal trajectory starts on the boundary of the moving set. The efficiency of the obtained results is illustrated by some examples related to practical modeling.
tldr: The paper develops necessary optimality conditions for a broad class of optimal control problems governed by constrained sweeping processes with controlled prox-regular moving sets and variable (free) time.
motivation: Sweeping processes model evolution of constrained dynamical systems and appear in mechanics, hysteresis, and contact problems, but optimal control formulations with prox-regular moving sets and variable time lacked a complete variational theory.
method: The authors use the method of discrete approximations to build a parametric family of discrete-time controlled sweeping processes, reduce them to nondynamic mathematical programs, and apply first- and second-order variational analysis and generalized differentiation (coderivatives) before passing to the continuous-time limit.
result: They obtain novel necessary optimality conditions for local minimizers of continuous-time controlled sweeping processes, featuring absolutely continuous and BV adjoint arcs, local/global maximization conditions, active-set multipliers, vector measures from constraints, and a free-time transversality condition via an averaged Hamiltonian, including nondegenerate forms.
conclusion: The derived conditions extend optimal control theory to prox-regular sweeping dynamics with variable time and are illustrated on practical modeling examples.

title: A $1/2$-Approximation For Pandora's Problem With Deadlines
authors: Shenyu Qin, Chihao Zhang, Yuhao Zhang, Zixuan Zhu
abstract: ArXiv:2610.13775v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Pandora's problem is a fundamental model of sequential search in which opening each box incurs a cost. We study the variant with deadlines, where each box has a publicly known deadline for both opening and selection. We prove that a simple threshold strategy achieves a [MATH]-approximation to the optimal expected utility, improving the previous guarantee of [MATH] due to Berger et al. (AAAI 2024).
tldr: The paper gives a 1/2-approximation algorithm for Pandora's problem with deadlines, improving on a previous guarantee by Berger et al.
motivation: Pandora's problem models sequential search with inspection costs, and the deadline variant captures settings where boxes must be opened and selected within publicly known time limits.
method: The authors analyze a simple threshold strategy and prove it achieves a constant-factor approximation to the optimal expected utility.
result: The proposed threshold strategy yields a 1/2-approximation, improving the earlier bound of Berger et al. (AAAI 2024).
conclusion: The work advances the theory of optimal stopping/sequential search with deadlines, a purely classical algorithmic problem with no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Insurance Perspectives On Climate-related Risks
authors: Michelle Dong, Aaron Bruhn, Francis K. C. Hui, Han Lin Shang
abstract: ArXiv:2610.12473v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Emerging climate risks are bringing pressing challenges for insurers globally, as they face growing uncertainty in quantifying climate impacts from physical and transition risks. Climate risks are broad and can manifest through short-term changes and events, as well as long-term and sometimes irreversible changes, such as sea level rise and temperature increases. Significant economic changes are inevitable as countries transition and adapt to mitigate climate-related risks. Given the wide range of potential implications for insurers, we conducted a series of interviews with insurance practitioners and academic researchers to explore the diverse landscape of current perspectives on climate-related risks. The interviews considered how insurers can manage emerging climate risks and the role of pricing as a signal of risk. In the context of unknown unknowns for insurers in understanding long-term impacts of climate change, we identify the importance of scenario analysis in informing forward-looking drivers of change and the importance it plays in meeting evolving regulatory requirements.
tldr: An interview-based study of insurance practitioners and academic researchers exploring how insurers perceive and manage emerging climate-related physical and transition risks.
motivation: Climate change introduces deep uncertainty for insurers in quantifying physical and transition risks, motivating a need to understand current industry perspectives and pricing signals.
method: The authors conducted a series of qualitative interviews with insurance practitioners and academic researchers to survey the landscape of views on climate risk management.
result: The interviews highlight the role of pricing as a risk signal and identify scenario analysis as key for informing forward-looking change and meeting evolving regulatory requirements under unknown unknowns.
conclusion: Insurers should rely on scenario analysis to navigate long-term, irreversible climate impacts and align with regulatory expectations, though many impacts remain deeply uncertain.

title: Learning Social Influence With Unobserved Attention
authors: William Thompson, Moyi Tian, Linh Huynh, Alexander Wiedemann, Vicki Modisette, Philip S. Chodrow, Heather Z. Brooks
abstract: ArXiv:2610.12616v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Social influence, the tendency of our social environment to sway our beliefs and behaviors, is often cited as a driver of population-level trends in opinions or beliefs. Many quantitative theories of social influence assume that an agent interacts with its entire social environment. This assumption is often unrealistic. For example, users of online platforms typically see posts from only a small subset of the accounts they follow at any given time. We introduce a simple probabilistic agent-based model of social influence that explicitly models unobserved attention mechanisms. The first of these latent mechanisms is selection: each agent interacts with only one other agent at a time from its social environment. The second is retention: the agent chooses whether or not to ignore the opinion of the other. Our model admits an efficient maximum-likelihood algorithm which allows us to fit it to opinion traces even when these mechanisms are unobserved. On synthetic data, omitting either latent mechanism reduces the overall strength of social influence governed by the inferred interaction kernel, which hides the evidence for the underlying nonlinearity of the social influence. We study a selection of previously analyzed empirical datasets and curate several new ones. We show that models that include the latent mechanisms are often more predictive on these datasets; indeed, they typically improve prediction far more than the choice of interaction kernel does. Modeling latent attention increases held-out predictive likelihood on 14 of these 15 datasets. Each mechanism changes the size of the inferred kernel in a predictable direction, while its effect on the kernel's shape depends on the data.
tldr: The paper introduces a probabilistic agent-based model of social influence that explicitly accounts for unobserved attention mechanisms—selection and retention—and fits it to opinion traces via maximum likelihood.
motivation: Many quantitative theories of social influence unrealistically assume that agents interact with their entire social environment, whereas online platform users typically attend to only a small subset of available information.
method: The authors develop a simple probabilistic agent-based model with latent selection (interacting with one agent at a time) and retention (choosing to ignore an opinion), and derive an efficient maximum-likelihood algorithm for fitting the model even when these mechanisms are unobserved.
result: On synthetic data, omitting either latent mechanism weakens inferred social influence and hides nonlinearity; on 14 of 15 empirical datasets, including the latent mechanisms improves held-out predictive likelihood more than the choice of interaction kernel does.
conclusion: Modeling unobserved attention mechanisms is important for accurately inferring social influence kernels, and the proposed framework offers a practical way to do so from opinion traces.

title: On The 100% Rule Of Linear Programming
authors: Jon Lee Marcia Fampa
abstract: ArXiv:2610.12665v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The so-called ``100% rule'' is a somewhat classical and yet somehow obscure rule that gives some local sensitivity-analysis information based on the very limited local sensitivity-analysis information that is often made available by linear-programming software, derived from an optimal basis that is hidden from the user. Introduced in a classic undergraduate textbook in 1977, half a century ago, it was only picked up on by researchers in a very limited way, and while it appears in some undergraduate textbooks, it tends not to appear in most modern graduate-level textbooks. Our contributions are to celebrate and revive interest in the 100% rule and to extend it in a meaningful way. We introduce a cone rule that certifies primal feasibility for more right-hand sides than the 100% rule does, using the same information, and that can be applied in linear time. We then study when this cone rule is tight, that is, when it captures the entire cone of right-hand sides for which the basis remains feasible. We characterize tightness in every dimension for right-hand sides interior to that cone, make the characterization explicit for m=2 and m=3, and settle the question for tridiagonal bases in every dimension: tightness is impossible once m>=4, and for m=3 we give an explicit criterion in the entries of the basis. We give further results for symmetric, integer and unimodular bases. Finally, when tightness fails, we measure the fraction of the feasibility cone captured by the rule using normalized solid angles. For the autoregressive family at m=3, we obtain a closed-form candidate for the infimum of this fraction over all right-hand sides, whose optimality is supported numerically. We also obtain a closed-form expression for the best case over most of the correlation range, subject to two numerically verified properties, and estimate the best-case value numerically more generally.
tldr: The paper revisits and extends the classical 100% rule in linear programming sensitivity analysis by introducing a cone rule that certifies primal feasibility for more right-hand sides using the same information.
motivation: The 100% rule, introduced in 1977, is a classical but obscure local sensitivity-analysis tool, and the authors aim to revive interest and provide a meaningful extension.
method: The authors introduce a cone rule for certifying primal feasibility of a fixed optimal basis under right-hand side perturbations, characterize its tightness across dimensions, and analyze the fraction of the feasibility cone captured using normalized solid angles.
result: The cone rule can be applied in linear time and is tight in some cases; tightness is characterized for m=2 and m=3, shown impossible for tridiagonal bases with m>=4, and further results are given for symmetric, integer, and unimodular bases.
conclusion: The work extends the 100% rule and provides new sensitivity-analysis results, but it is purely a linear programming contribution with no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Childcare Waitlists
authors: Yueyang Zhong, Jun Li, Senthil Veeraraghavan
abstract: ArXiv:2610.12732v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Parents seeking childcare often face long waitlists. At the same time, vacancies at childcare centers can remain unfilled for extended periods. We trace this paradox to two persistent features of childcare services. First, families consider multiple child care options due to enrollment uncertainties, resulting in phantom listings that remain on waitlists even after families have found care elsewhere or no longer need a slot. Second, filling a slot is time-consuming: centers learn whether a family is actively seeking enrollment only after making an offer and waiting for a response. As families pursue alternatives while they wait and their children age, these delays and feedback effects amplify the mismatch between demand and available capacity. We study two operational remedies. First, we examine regular verification that removes phantom listings before offers are made, improving the efficiency of enrollment and reducing vacancies. Second, we study mixed-age classrooms, in which some slots designated for older children can be flexibly used by younger children. This flexibility increases utilization, shortens waits, and reduces wasted offers. Its benefits extend beyond conventional pooling: as children move between age groups, classrooms can be filled through internal flows rather than costly external search, further reducing enrollment delays. Together, verification and mixed use offer a way to expand effective capacity in early childhood classrooms, where regulatory and operational constraints make adding physical capacity particularly costly.
tldr: The paper analyzes operational remedies for childcare waitlist inefficiencies caused by phantom listings and delayed enrollment feedback.
motivation: Parents face long waitlists while childcare vacancies remain unfilled, a paradox driven by enrollment uncertainty and slow offer-response dynamics.
method: The authors model waitlist dynamics with phantom listings and delayed feedback, then study regular verification of active demand and mixed-age classroom flexibility as operational remedies.
result: Verification removes phantom listings and improves enrollment efficiency, while mixed-age classrooms increase utilization, shorten waits, and reduce wasted offers through internal flows.
conclusion: Verification and mixed-use policies can effectively expand childcare capacity without costly physical expansion, addressing regulatory and operational constraints.

title: A Lipschitz Refinement Of The Bebutov-Kakutani Dynamical Embedding Theorem For Connected Lie Group Actions
authors: Yonatan Gutman, Qiang Huo, Kangbo Ouyang
abstract: ArXiv:2610.13091v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let [MATH] be a connected Lie group equipped with a compatible right-invariant metric and let [MATH] act continuously on a compact metrizable space [MATH]. We prove that [MATH] admits a [MATH]-equivariant embedding into the right argument shift action on the space of one-Lipschitz maps from [MATH] to [MATH] if and only if the set of fixed points topologically embeds into [MATH]. This generalizes a theorem proved by Gutman, Huo and Tsukamoto for [MATH]-flows.
tldr: The paper proves a Lipschitz-equivariant refinement of the Bebutov-Kakutani dynamical embedding theorem for continuous actions of connected Lie groups on compact metrizable spaces.
motivation: Dynamical embedding theorems aim to realize abstract topological dynamical systems inside concrete shift-like actions; the authors seek a metric (Lipschitz) strengthening for general connected Lie group actions beyond the previously handled R-flows.
method: Using a compatible right-invariant metric on a connected Lie group, the authors construct an equivariant embedding into the right argument shift action on the space of one-Lipschitz maps, characterizing embeddability via topological embeddability of the fixed-point set.
result: They establish that such a Lipschitz equivariant embedding exists if and only if the set of fixed points of the action topologically embeds into the target space, generalizing the earlier theorem of Gutman, Huo and Tsukamoto for R-flows.
conclusion: The work extends the Bebutov-Kakutani embedding program to connected Lie group actions with Lipschitz control, contributing to topological dynamics and ergodic theory rather than quantum information science.

title: Towards Safe World Models: Risks, Defenses, And Evaluation
authors: Xiaoma Wang, Litian Zhang, Xinze Shi, Zhengxuan Hu, Zihan Yang, Mingqi Ren, You Wu, Bingyu Yan, Zelong Yu, Zhenjie Su, Yuming Shang, Xi Zhang, Chaozhuo Li, Philip S. Yu
abstract: ArXiv:2610.13372v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: World models support planning, control, learning from imagined experience, and model-mediated evaluation by predicting action-conditioned consequences. Their safety cannot be inferred from predictive accuracy alone: errors in observations, state and memory, dynamics, evaluation, execution, or feedback can propagate into unsafe decisions and persist through updates. This work organizes the literature on world-model safety around a six-stage lifecycle covering data and observations, state and memory, dynamics and imagination, evaluation and planning, action and control, and feedback and update. We synthesize non-adversarial failures, attacks, defenses, evaluation protocols, benchmarks, and deployment conditions, and distinguish evidence directness from outcome level. The current evidence corpus contains 163 cited works. We use the framework to identify where claims are supported, where attribution remains unresolved, and which measurements are needed to connect model-level behavior to closed-loop and operational safety.
tldr: A literature review organizing world-model safety research around a six-stage lifecycle, synthesizing failures, attacks, defenses, and evaluation protocols.
motivation: World models are increasingly used for planning and control, but their safety cannot be inferred from predictive accuracy alone; this work aims to systematically map risks and defenses across the world-model lifecycle.
method: The authors survey and organize 163 cited works into a six-stage lifecycle covering data/observations, state/memory, dynamics/imagination, evaluation/planning, action/control, and feedback/update, distinguishing evidence directness and outcome levels.
result: The framework identifies where claims are supported, where attribution remains unresolved, and which measurements are needed to connect model-level behavior to closed-loop and operational safety.
conclusion: The paper provides a structured agenda for world-model safety, highlighting gaps and evaluation needs, but it is entirely outside quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Parallel Design Of A GPU-Resident Semi-Lagrangian Drift-Kinetic Solver On Unstructured Extruded Tokamak Meshes
authors: Mark F. Adams
abstract: ArXiv:2610.12585v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Semi-Lagrangian (SL) schemes advect a distribution function along characteristics and remap it to a fixed grid. They are unconditionally stable without a global solve, and with discontinuous Galerkin (DG) integration the transfer along a magnetic field line conserves mass exactly. This paper presents the parallel and GPU design of a 3X+2V SLDG drift-kinetic tokamak solver on unstructured, flux-surface-aligned poloidal planes of shaped cross section, extruded toroidally. Transport follows magnetic field lines across the planes, and each velocity channel advances a fixed distance per step, proportional to its parallel speed, so the halo depth a channel needs grows with its speed. Velocity-dependent ragged halos exploit this, sending each channel only its own upwind depth. The 4D decomposition includes the toroidal angle, the 2D poloidal plane and the magnetic moment, and leaves the parallel velocity whole: no stage transports across the magnetic moment, while a parallel-velocity partition would put a halo inside the acceleration stage. On NVIDIA A100s the design strong-scales over the magnetic-moment axis from one to 12 four-GPU nodes, and a weak series of three points refining all five phase-space dimensions together, 16x in total per series point, holds a weak-scaling efficiency of 75% on 16 GPUs and 57% on 256, from a one-GPU base case. The pointwise interpolations within the poloidal plane do not conserve mass, and the full step's mass drift stays below 2.1x10^-5 at every series point. The design was implemented with an AI code assistant under a machine-checked regression discipline, in which every change is held to one of four exactness classes, from bit-identical to a physics rate within a stated tolerance.
tldr: The paper presents a parallel GPU design for a semi-Lagrangian drift-kinetic solver on unstructured extruded tokamak meshes, focusing on performance and scalability.
motivation: Efficient numerical simulation of drift-kinetic plasma dynamics is important for tokamak fusion research, where high-dimensional phase-space solvers are computationally demanding.
method: The solver uses a 3X+2V semi-Lagrangian discontinuous Galerkin scheme with velocity-dependent ragged halos and a 4D decomposition over toroidal angle, poloidal plane, and magnetic moment, implemented on NVIDIA A100 GPUs with AI-assisted regression discipline.
result: The design strong-scales over the magnetic-moment axis from one to 12 four-GPU nodes, achieving 75% weak-scaling efficiency on 16 GPUs and 57% on 256 GPUs, while maintaining mass drift below 2.1e-5 at every weak-scaling point.
conclusion: The work demonstrates a scalable GPU implementation for drift-kinetic tokamak simulations, but it lies outside quantum information, information thermodynamics, quantum networks, and hybrid quantum systems.

title: A Volume-controlled Level-set Method For Topology Optimization
authors: Wei Gong, Zhenmin Zhang, Shengfeng Zhu
abstract: ArXiv:2610.12922v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Topology optimization typically involves a geometric volume/mass constraint due to the limited use of material. As a popular technique for topology optimization, the level-set method typically employs the Lagrange method, the penalty method, or the augmented Lagrangian approach to address the volume constraint. This requires careful parameter tuning and may lead to non-monotonic changes in the objective. In this paper, we present a new volume-controlled level-set method for topology optimization. By imposing a scalar weighted volume?compatibility constraint in a modified Stokes-type extension-regularization problem, the velocity is made volume compatible at the beginning of each frozen transport interval. At the continuous level, we prove that the initial rate of change of the regularized volume vanishes and that the subsequent frozen-velocity drift is of order [MATH]; under a narrow-band assumption, the corresponding constant is independent of the smoothing parameter. For the discontinuous Galerkin spatial semi-discretization of the level-set transport equation, we derive a quantitative regularized-volume drift estimate that displays the dependence on the smoothing parameter, spatial mesh size, transport time, and discrete velocity. The effectiveness of the present algorithm is demonstrated through the minimum compliance problem for linear elasticity, the eigenfrequency maximization for structural vibration, and the minimum energy dissipation problem for Stokes flows.
tldr: The paper introduces a volume-controlled level-set method for topology optimization with a modified Stokes-type extension-regularization problem.
motivation: Topology optimization often requires volume constraints, but standard Lagrange or penalty methods need parameter tuning and can cause non-monotonic objective changes.
method: A scalar weighted volume-compatibility constraint is imposed in a modified Stokes-type extension-regularization problem, and the discontinuous Galerkin semi-discretization of the level-set transport equation is analyzed.
result: The initial rate of change of regularized volume vanishes, frozen-velocity drift is of order given by the mesh and smoothing parameters, and numerical examples demonstrate effectiveness.
conclusion: The proposed method provides a volume-controlled level-set approach for topology optimization, with theoretical drift estimates and validation on compliance, eigenfrequency, and Stokes flow problems.

title: Finiteness Of Planar Central Configurations Of Five Bodies For All Positive Masses
authors: Tejasvi Singh Tomar
abstract: ArXiv:2610.13100v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that for every choice of five positive masses the planar five-body problem has finitely many central configurations up to similarity. This settles Smale's sixth problem for five bodies in the plane. Albouy and Kaloshin proved it for masses outside a closed algebraic subset of codimension two. We follow their method. Infinitely many central configurations would give an algebraic curve of complex solutions. At the places at infinity of the curve the valuations of the mutual distances must balance. We determine the possible valuation vectors at all positive masses, together with the mass conditions under which each can occur. We treat limits in which four bodies form a cluster of zero potential energy by expanding the potential, which is constant along the curve, at a place. This excludes, at every positive mass, one of the two diagrams in which such clusters occur, and part of the other. The same expansion excludes one further diagram at every positive mass. What remains is an exact analysis, by computer algebra, of the sets of mass conditions that can hold together at positive masses. Exact rational certificates show that the balance fails under each of them, except on a few one-parameter families of masses, which we treat separately. On the rays through [MATH] and [MATH] the certificates do not apply. On the first ray they cannot apply: there the complex equations have a continuum of solutions, as Albouy and Kaloshin observed. On these rays we count the real central configurations: there are 306 and 294 up to orientation-preserving similarity. The certificates, the programs that check them and a proof of the theorem in the Lean proof assistant are available.
tldr: The paper proves that for all positive masses, the planar five-body problem has finitely many central configurations up to similarity, settling Smale's sixth problem for five bodies.
motivation: Central configurations are key to understanding the dynamics of the N-body problem, and Smale's sixth problem asks about their finiteness for the five-body problem.
method: The authors follow the approach of Albouy and Kaloshin, using algebraic geometry, valuations at infinity, computer algebra certificates, and Lean formal verification to analyze possible mass conditions.
result: They rule out all but a few one-parameter families of masses where a continuum of complex solutions could occur, and on exceptional rays they count 306 and 294 real central configurations up to orientation-preserving similarity.
conclusion: The finiteness of planar central configurations for five arbitrary positive masses is established, resolving Smale's sixth problem in this case, with certificates and Lean proofs made available.

title: An Exploration Of Attacks On Ai Agent Systems
authors: Cathleen Qiao, Layah Vigneaud, Chloe Brandon, Max Cabilangan, Xiyuan Cao, Isaac Khabra, Reva Mahajan, Lena Nguyen, Kyle Pak, Anagh Pandya, Roshni Dave, Peiran Wang
abstract: ArXiv:2610.12524v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: As autonomous AI agents become more integrated into sensitive domains, it is crucial that single and multi-agent AI systems are secured. This paper investigates how prompt injection attacks can exploit both direct user inputs and inter?agent communication to leak sensitive information and trigger cross-agent infections. While our tests mostly highlight key vulnerabilities in single-agent systems, we also extend these attacks to multi-agent frameworks, investigating how weaknesses can propagate across agents. Our findings emphasize the need for more robust defenses as AI agents become more commonly embedded in real-world workflows.
tldr: This paper investigates prompt injection attacks on single- and multi-agent AI systems, focusing on information leakage and cross-agent infection.
motivation: As autonomous AI agents are increasingly deployed in sensitive domains, there is a pressing need to understand and mitigate security vulnerabilities in both single-agent and multi-agent frameworks.
method: The authors design and test prompt injection attacks that exploit direct user inputs and inter-agent communication, then extend these attacks to multi-agent settings to study propagation.
result: The tests reveal key vulnerabilities in single-agent systems and demonstrate how weaknesses can propagate across agents in multi-agent frameworks.
conclusion: The findings highlight the need for more robust defenses as AI agents become embedded in real-world workflows.

title: Vulnerable Models In The Ai Supply Chain: An Empirical Study Of Adoption, Propagation, And Usage Patterns
authors: The Anh Nguyen, Triet Huynh Minh Le, M. Ali Babar
abstract: ArXiv:2610.12893v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The rapid integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) models has established a complex supply chain, but many of these shared artifacts harbor severe vulnerabilities such as insecure serialization and architectural backdoors. While prior efforts have extensively scanned model registries to flag malicious artifacts, a critical gap remains in understanding how developers actually adopt and integrate these unsafe models into downstream software systems. We bridge this gap by conducting a large-scale empirical study on the usage and propagation of 16,977 known vulnerable models on HuggingFace flagged by InsightDB. We track their prevalence across GitHub repositories, software packages, fine-tuning chains, and deployed applications. Our analysis reveals that, despite being publicly flagged, these vulnerable models appear in over 21,000 code locations across more than 5,000 open-source repositories, with 3,757 distinct flagged models (22.1\%) actively referenced in at least one project. To understand how these models are integrated in code and identify recurring usage patterns, we categorize and analyze the recurring patterns surrounding them via a customized pipeline that combines Code Property Graphs extraction with a tailored Frequent Subgraph Mining approach. Across all patterns, we find no evidence of provenance verification or model sanitization logic, with developers frequently bypassing security parameters or delegating trust to permissive framework defaults. These findings underscore that scanning model files alone is insufficient, highlighting the urgent need for context-aware security analysis and stricter integration guardrails at the application layer of the AI supply chain.
tldr: A large-scale empirical study tracking how known vulnerable AI models from HuggingFace are adopted and propagated into downstream software repositories and applications.
motivation: AI models form a complex supply chain where shared artifacts can carry severe vulnerabilities, but little is known about how developers actually adopt and integrate unsafe models into downstream software.
method: The authors analyze 16,977 flagged vulnerable models on HuggingFace, tracking their usage across GitHub repositories, packages, fine-tuning chains, and deployed applications, and use Code Property Graphs with frequent subgraph mining to identify recurring integration patterns.
result: Vulnerable models appear in over 21,000 code locations across more than 5,000 open-source repositories, with 22.1% of flagged models actively referenced, and no evidence of provenance verification or model sanitization, with developers often bypassing security parameters.
conclusion: Scanning model files alone is insufficient; context-aware security analysis and stricter integration guardrails are needed at the application layer of the AI supply chain.

title: Cancerous Backdoor Attack: Gradual Activation Via Invisible Tokens And A Stage Controller
authors: Tahmid Imtiaz Imu, Emama Nahid, Prodipta Sen Amartya, Ahsanul Jobayer, Yutong Song, Jiang Wu, Pengfei Zhang, Honghui Xu
abstract: ArXiv:2610.12644v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Backdoor Attacks on Large Language Models (LLMs) typically follow a trigger-response pattern, where satisfying a trigger condition activates a single terminal behavior. However, this single-point backdoor activation does not explore attacks in which malicious behavior develops gradually through multiple intermediate stages before reaching the terminal activation stage. We present Cancerous Backdoor Attack, that gradually corrupts an LLM's reasoning over a sequence of interactions by leveraging invisible tokens and a stage controller. Specifically, invisible tokens provide hidden stages to the model without appearing in the user's visible request and the stage controller tracks the attack's progression during inference to realize gradual activation. We evaluate Cancerous Backdoor Attack across several reasoning datasets. The attack consistently produces gradual reasoning corruption across models and tasks. We compare Cancerous Backdoor Attack with prior backdoor attack baselines to demonstrate our proposed attack outperforms the baselines. Our results indicate that reasoning corruption can develop gradually before it becomes visible, making answer accuracy alone insufficient for detecting backdoor attacks.
tldr: The paper introduces a gradual backdoor attack on LLMs that uses invisible tokens and a stage controller to corrupt reasoning over multiple interactions.
motivation: Prior backdoor attacks activate a single terminal behavior upon a trigger, leaving gradual multi-stage malicious development unexplored.
method: Invisible tokens encode hidden stages in prompts without appearing in the visible user request, while a stage controller tracks and advances the attack during inference.
result: The attack consistently produces gradual reasoning corruption across several reasoning datasets and models, outperforming prior backdoor baselines.
conclusion: Reasoning corruption can develop gradually and invisibly, so answer accuracy alone is insufficient for detecting backdoor attacks.

title: Pulsed Control Of An Entanglement-breaking Index: Thermal Valleys, A Certified Valve, And Its Open-close Asymmetry
authors: Eran Kopel
abstract: ArXiv:2610.13135v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The entanglement-breaking index of a channel is the number of self-compositions after which all entanglement with a reference system is destroyed. In a thermal qubit collision loop whose round is affine in the bath polarisation p, some circuits have thermal valleys: on an interior window of p the index falls below its infinite-temperature value. Rounds at different p compose exactly, so every schedule of polarisations defines a composite channel whose entanglement-breaking status can be certified in ball arithmetic. A gated search of 33 million random circuits finds no valley with contrast above about 3e-3, with an interior maximum near index 90, and yields six certified targets. At the reference target, held inside its window for 88 rounds, a centred excursion to p = 0.05 restores entanglement at exactly eight rounds: every shorter centred pulse certifiably fails, and so do the same eight rounds at the start. A 53-round pulse certifiably beats the static protocol, a depth-three valley is walked down its staircase by pulse duration, and a 1.2 per cent coherent tilt of the ancilla opens the switch at fixed population. Closing the switch costs 21 to 35 rounds. The asymmetry is not one of local rates, which agree to within about two per cent at matched circuit positions (certified). It is one of distance and response: closing must remove an entanglement margin 2.2 times larger, and while hot rounds added to a window hold act almost independently, window rounds added to a hot hold act collectively. Near the crossing, the lever of the log-margin is that of a linear approach to the entanglement-breaking boundary, with no free parameter. At the reference target, depolarising noise of about [MATH] per round kills a signature of size [MATH] read after [MATH] rounds: 1.3e-4 for the static signal, 6.5e-6 for the eight-round switch.
tldr: Analysis failed

title: Dimension Theory Of Group Actions By Circle Diffeomorphisms I: Stationary Measures
authors: Weikun He, Yuxiang Jiao, Disheng Xu
abstract: ArXiv:2610.13254v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish a structure theorem for smooth random walks on the circle and study the dimensional properties of their stationary measures, including exact dimensionality and a Ledrappier-Young-type dimension formula. These results provide the technical tools needed for the main theorems in Part II "Dimension theory of group actions by circle diffeomorphisms II: Minimal sets". They also yield an approximation theorem in the spirit of Katok, Avila-Crovisier-Wilkinson, and Morris-Shmerkin, together with a time-reversal symmetry for circle actions: every semigroup [MATH] contained in [MATH] without finite orbits has the same number of minimal sets as its inverse semigroup [MATH].
tldr: The paper establishes a structure theorem for smooth random walks on the circle and studies the dimensional properties of their stationary measures, including exact dimensionality and a Ledrappier-Young-type dimension formula.
motivation: The results provide technical tools for the main theorems in Part II on dimension theory of group actions by circle diffeomorphisms, and yield an approximation theorem and time-reversal symmetry for circle actions.
method: The authors analyze smooth random walks on the circle, deriving a structure theorem and dimension formulas for stationary measures.
result: They prove exact dimensionality and a Ledrappier-Young-type dimension formula, an approximation theorem, and a time-reversal symmetry relating the number of minimal sets of a semigroup and its inverse.
conclusion: The work advances the dimension theory of group actions by circle diffeomorphisms, with applications to minimal sets and approximation results.

title: Complexity Of Autobidding Equilibria In Gsp Sponsored Shopping
authors: Kristoffer Arnsfelt Hansen, Yuhao Li, Xinhao Nie
abstract: ArXiv:2610.13716v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We revisit autobidding equilibria in GSP sponsored shopping auctions, recently proposed and studied in D\"utting et al. On the existence side, we show that autobidding equilibria under both budget constraints (ABE-B) and return-on-investment constraints (ABE-R) always exist and, moreover, always admit equilibria with polynomial-size support over the allocation space. On the computational side, we show that computing an exact equilibrium is in FIXP, and that computing an approximate equilibrium is in PPAD. We also prove that computing an approximate equilibrium is PPAD-hard for both ABE-B and ABE-R. Together, these results provide a fairly comprehensive picture of the computational complexity of autobidding equilibria in GSP sponsored shopping auctions.
tldr: The paper studies the existence and computational complexity of autobidding equilibria in GSP sponsored shopping auctions, showing polynomial-support existence and PPAD-completeness/FIXP membership results.
motivation: Autobidding has become a central mechanism in online advertising, but the equilibrium properties of GSP sponsored shopping auctions under budget and return-on-investment constraints remain poorly understood.
method: The authors analyze autobidding equilibria (ABE-B and ABE-R) using game-theoretic and complexity-theoretic tools, proving existence with polynomial support and classifying exact and approximate equilibrium computation via FIXP and PPAD.
result: They show that equilibria always exist for both budget and ROI constraints, with polynomial-size support; exact computation is in FIXP, approximate computation is in PPAD, and approximate computation is PPAD-hard.
conclusion: The work provides a fairly comprehensive complexity-theoretic picture of autobidding equilibria in GSP sponsored shopping auctions, with hardness results and containment in FIXP/PPAD.
